questions.stem: A microbiologist samples decaying leaf litter from a forest floor and isolates a filamentous fungus that grows readily on the dead plant material. Most fungi obtain their energy in which of the following ways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absorption of nutrients from decomposing dead organic material

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixation of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia for biosynthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obligate intracellular replication within living host cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxidation of inorganic sulfur compounds present in the soil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Photosynthesis using chlorophyll contained within the hyphae

explanation.summary: Most fungi are saprophytes that feed on decomposing dead organic material.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that obtain energy from other animals and plants. The majority are saprophytes, meaning they feed on decomposing, dead organic material, which is why they are essential in ecosystems for turning over organic matter. Like bacteria, most fungi are harmless or even helpful to humans.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nitrogen fixation is a bacterial capability and is not how fungi meet their energy needs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fungi are not obligate intracellular organisms; most live freely in soil and decaying matter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxidizing inorganic sulfur is a bacterial lifestyle; fungi digest organic material instead.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fungi contain no chlorophyll and do not photosynthesize; they take their energy from other organisms.

questions.stem: A student examining stained fungal hyphae under the microscope sees regularly spaced cross-walls that divide each filament into segments. Which of the following best describes these structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attachment organelles that anchor the mycelium to the substrate surface

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breaks in the hyphae that let macromolecules and organelles pass between segments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Membrane pores through which ergosterol is exported to the cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rigid plugs that permanently isolate each hyphal segment from its neighbors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Specialized sites where conidia are assembled before release into the air

explanation.summary: Septa are breaks within hyphae that allow macromolecules and even organelles to flow between hyphal segments.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyphae may contain septa, which are breaks throughout the hyphae that allow macromolecules and even organelles to flow between hyphal segments. Some fungi do not have septa at all, so the presence or absence of septa is one useful way to tell fungi apart in the laboratory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Septa have no anchoring role; hyphae themselves extend into the substrate for nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Septa are structural breaks in the hyphae, not transport pores for sterols.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Septa do not seal segments off; material moves across them between hyphal compartments.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidia are produced by spore-producing structures, not by the septa within a hypha.

questions.stem: A fungal colony is spreading outward across an agar plate through branching filamentous structures. These structures serve which of the following primary functions for the colony?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Converting host cholesterol into ergosterol for membrane synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixing carbon dioxide into sugars distributed through the mycelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Producing antibodies that neutralize competing bacterial species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reaching into the environment and secreting enzymes that digest nutrients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Storing dormant conidia until ambient temperature reaches 37°C

explanation.summary: Hyphae extend into the environment to find nutrients, then secrete enzymes that break those nutrients down for absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungi live in colonies called mycelia that are connected by vegetative hyphae, which are branching filamentous structures. Hyphae reach out into the environment for nutrients to absorb and secrete enzymes that break those nutrients down for easier digestion. Hyphae also participate in fungal sexual reproduction by fusing with one another.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fungi synthesize their own ergosterol and do not depend on converting host cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbon fixation is a plant and cyanobacterial process; fungi absorb preformed organic nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fungi do not make antibodies; antibody production is a function of the host adaptive immune system.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidia break off and disperse rather than being warehoused in hyphae until a temperature threshold.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus undergoes debridement of a necrotic sinus lesion. Histologic sections of the tissue show broad, branching hyphae that contain no cross-walls. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Mucor spp. are opportunistic fungi whose hyphae are aseptate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both Mucor spp. and Aspergillus spp. are opportunist fungi that cause severe disease in immunocompromised hosts, and they are distinguished on histology by their hyphae. Mucor spp. have aseptate hyphae, meaning the filaments lack the cross-walls seen in other molds. Finding branching hyphae without septa therefore points to Mucor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. have septate hyphae, so visible cross-walls would be expected in the tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis appears in tissue as a thick-walled budding yeast rather than as hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans is a dimorphic organism that is a component of normal flora, not an aseptate mold in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum appears in tissue as a budding yeast, not as broad aseptate hyphae.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman receiving induction chemotherapy for leukemia develops fever and a cavitary lung lesion. Lung biopsy shows branching filamentous hyphae that are divided at regular intervals by cross-walls. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryptococcus spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Aspergillus spp. are opportunistic fungi with septate hyphae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus spp. are opportunistic fungi that cause severe disease in the immunocompromised, and their hyphae are septate. The cross-walls seen in this biopsy are the septa that distinguish Aspergillus from the aseptate molds. Presence or absence of septa is a key morphologic discriminator between these look-alike opportunists.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis appears in tissue as a broad-based budding yeast, not as hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus spp. are exogenous yeasts rather than septate molds in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum is seen in tissue as a small budding yeast, not as septate hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. have aseptate hyphae, so the regular cross-walls described here argue against it.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role that conidia play in fungal biology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They anchor the mycelium to decomposing organic substrate

choices.label: B
choices.text: They form the rigid outer layer of the fungal cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: They fuse with a second hypha to create a binucleated cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: They secrete keratinase to digest the stratum corneum

choices.label: E
choices.text: They travel through air and water to establish new colonies

explanation.summary: Conidia are fungal spores that break off the mycelium and disperse through air and water to found new colonies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Conidia can break off from the mycelium and use air and water to travel to new locations and start a new fungal colony, which is a critical way fungi spread. In human infection, we either inhale these conidia or have them land on our skin. Because bacteria also form spores, fungal spores are given the separate name conidia to minimize confusion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anchoring and nutrient absorption in the substrate are functions of the vegetative hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The rigid outer layer of the fungal cell is the cell wall built of β-glucans and chitin, not conidia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fusion of two hyphae to form a binucleated cell is plasmogamy, a function of hyphae rather than conidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratinase production is a property of dermatophytes invading skin, not a general role of conidia.

questions.stem: A mycology laboratory is characterizing the spores released from a mold colony. Fungal conidia are best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binucleated cells produced immediately after cytoplasmic fusion occurs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diploid cells that are metabolically active and require enriched media

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dormant bacterial endospores acquired from contaminating normal flora

choices.label: D
choices.text: Haploid cells with few metabolic demands that withstand tough environments

choices.label: E
choices.text: Multinucleate hyphal fragments that have shed their surrounding cell wall

explanation.summary: Conidia are specialized haploid cells optimized for transport: mobile, metabolically undemanding, and hardy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungal spores are specialized haploid cells optimized for transportation. They are mobile, have few metabolic demands, and are able to withstand tough environments, which is what makes them effective vehicles for spreading a fungus to new locations. These fungal spores are termed conidia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A binucleated cell arises from plasmogamy between hyphae, which is a separate step from conidium formation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conidia are haploid and metabolically undemanding rather than diploid and nutritionally fastidious.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conidia are fungal, not bacterial; the separate name exists precisely to avoid confusion with bacterial spores.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidia are discrete walled cells, not wall-less fragments broken off from a hypha.

questions.stem: A soil isolate is grown at 25°C and stained with lactophenol blue. Microscopy of the mold shows both small conidia and distinctly large conidia that have a sun-like appearance. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Histoplasma capsulatum makes both microconidia and macroconidia, and its macroconidia have a distinctive large, sun-like appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Conidia can be small (microconidia) or large (macroconidia), and a given fungus may produce one type or both. Histoplasma capsulatum possesses both microconidia and macroconidia, and its macroconidia are distinct, with a large, sun-like appearance. The type and appearance of conidia is one of the features used to distinguish fungi in the laboratory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. are recognized by septate hyphae rather than by large sun-like macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis possesses only microconidia, so large sun-like macroconidia would not be seen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans grows as a budding yeast whose form depends on nutrients and pH, not as a conidia-bearing mold.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. are identified by their aseptate hyphae, not by a pair of distinctive conidial sizes.

questions.stem: A thermally dimorphic fungus isolated from a patient's respiratory specimen is grown at room temperature. Microscopy of the mold phase shows only small conidia; no large conidia are present. Which of the following organisms best fits this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryptococcus spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Blastomyces dermatitidis possesses only microconidia, which separates it from Histoplasma capsulatum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blastomyces dermatitidis and Histoplasma capsulatum are both thermally dimorphic and can be told apart by their conidia. Blastomyces dermatitidis possesses only microconidia, whereas Histoplasma capsulatum possesses both microconidia and macroconidia. Finding small conidia alone in the mold phase therefore favors Blastomyces.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida albicans is dimorphic on the basis of nutrients and pH, not temperature, and is not a conidia-forming mold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus spp. are exogenous yeasts and are not among the thermally dimorphic conidia-formers described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum would also show its distinctive large, sun-like macroconidia alongside the microconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. are not thermally dimorphic and are identified by their aseptate hyphae.

questions.stem: During sexual reproduction in fungi, cells from two genetically independent hyphae fuse so that the resulting single cell contains one nucleus from each parent hypha. This step is called which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Germination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Karyogamy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meiosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plasmogamy

explanation.summary: Plasmogamy is the fusion of cytoplasm from two hyphae, creating a binucleated (dikaryotic) cell.
explanation.whyCorrect: In fungal sexual reproduction, cells from two different hyphae fuse to form a binucleated cell in a step called plasmogamy, with one nucleus contributed by each genetically independent hypha. The cell at this point is dikaryotic (n + n) because the two nuclei have not yet merged.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding is a mode of asexual division in yeasts and involves only one parent cell.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Germination is the later process in which dispersed conidia form new mycelia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Karyogamy is fusion of the two nuclei into a diploid zygote, which follows plasmogamy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meiosis occurs after nuclear fusion and generates the conidia that are subsequently dispersed.

questions.stem: Two fungal hyphae have fused, and the resulting cell is now dikaryotic (n + n). Which of the following events occurs next, and what is its immediate product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding, producing a haploid (n) daughter yeast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Germination, producing a binucleated (n + n) conidium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Karyogamy, producing a diploid (2n) zygote

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meiosis, producing a dikaryotic (n + n) hypha

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plasmogamy, producing a diploid (2n) zygote

explanation.summary: After plasmogamy creates a dikaryotic cell, karyogamy fuses the two nuclei into a diploid zygote.
explanation.whyCorrect: Plasmogamy produces a binucleated, dikaryotic (n + n) cell, and the two nuclei then fuse to form a diploid zygote in the step called karyogamy. Meiosis follows to form conidia, which disperse and germinate so that new mycelia form. This exchange of genetic information lets two fungi produce offspring distinct from either parent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding is an asexual mode of yeast division and is not part of this sexual sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Germination is the final step in which dispersed conidia form new mycelia, not the step after plasmogamy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meiosis comes after karyogamy and yields haploid conidia rather than a dikaryotic hypha.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasmogamy is the step that already occurred, and it produces a dikaryotic cell rather than a zygote.

questions.stem: A thermally dimorphic fungus takes which of the following forms at 25°C and at 37°C, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conidium at 25°C and hyphal cyst at 37°C

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mold at 25°C and mold at 37°C

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mold at 25°C and yeast at 37°C

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yeast at 25°C and mold at 37°C

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast at 25°C and yeast at 37°C

explanation.summary: Thermally dimorphic fungi are molds at room temperature and budding yeasts at body temperature.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thermally dimorphic fungi are molds at room or ambient temperatures (25°C) and single-celled budding yeasts at human body temperature (37°C). The mnemonic used to remember this is "mold in the cold, yeast in the heat." Histoplasma capsulatum and Blastomyces dermatitidis both display this thermal dimorphism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dimorphism refers to the mold and yeast forms, not to conidia converting into a cyst stage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A single mold form at both temperatures would mean the organism is not dimorphic at all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the relationship; the yeast form appears at body temperature, not at room temperature.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single yeast form at both temperatures would likewise mean the organism is not thermally dimorphic.

questions.stem: A laboratory receives a specimen from a patient with suspected blastomycosis and inoculates two sets of culture plates, one incubated at room temperature and one at body temperature. Which of the following best explains the purpose of incubating at two temperatures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To confirm that the isolate produces β-1,3-glucan synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: To demonstrate both the mold form and the yeast form of the fungus

choices.label: C
choices.text: To determine whether the isolate is endogenous or exogenous flora

choices.label: D
choices.text: To distinguish septate hyphae from aseptate hyphae within tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: To measure the minimum inhibitory concentration of amphotericin B

explanation.summary: Thermally dimorphic fungi are cultured at both room and body temperature so that both their distinct mold and yeast forms can be seen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma capsulatum and Blastomyces dermatitidis both display thermal dimorphism. For laboratory diagnosis they are grown at both room and body temperature, because the mold form and the yeast form are each distinct and recognizable. Seeing both morphologies from the same isolate supports the identification.

whyWrongByChoice.A: β-1,3-glucan synthase is an antifungal drug target and is not assayed by dual-temperature incubation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endogenous versus exogenous refers to whether the fungus is normal flora, which culture temperature does not address.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Septation is assessed by microscopy of hyphae, not by comparing growth at two temperatures.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Susceptibility testing is a separate function of culture and does not require two incubation temperatures.

questions.stem: Candida albicans is a dimorphic fungus, yet it is not grouped with the thermally dimorphic fungi. Which of the following best explains why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It grows only as a budding yeast and never adopts any other form

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a soil organism acquired only by inhaling airborne conidia

choices.label: C
choices.text: It lacks ergosterol and therefore cannot remodel its cell membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reproduces exclusively by symmetric fission rather than by budding

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its form is set by pH, nutrients, temperature, and the immune response

explanation.summary: Candida albicans is dimorphic, but its form is determined by several factors, not temperature alone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most dimorphic fungi are thermally dimorphic, switching between mold at room temperature and yeast at body temperature. Candida albicans is also dimorphic, but its form is determined by pH, nutrients, temperature, and the immune response rather than by temperature alone. Because temperature is not the sole determinant, it is not classified with the thermally dimorphic fungi.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida albicans is explicitly dimorphic, so describing it as locked into a single yeast form is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida spp. are part of normal human flora and cause endogenous infection rather than being inhaled soil organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ergosterol is present in fungal membranes generally, and its presence is unrelated to the dimorphism classification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yeasts may divide by budding or fission, and neither mode explains Candida's exclusion from thermal dimorphism.

questions.stem: Lung tissue from a 41-year-old man is stained and examined. The yeast cells present have walls that appear notably thick, and each daughter cell divides from its parent across a wide attachment. Which of the following organisms is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Blastomyces dermatitidis yeast bud from the parent cell across a thick base, described as broad-based budding.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yeast forms of Blastomyces dermatitidis and Histoplasma capsulatum are distinguished by how the individual cells bud during mitosis. In Blastomyces dermatitidis, new yeast cells bud from parent cells with a thick base, referred to as broad-based budding, and the cell membrane also appears thicker than that of Histoplasma capsulatum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. appear in tissue as septate hyphae rather than as budding yeast cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans is an endogenous organism of normal flora and is not identified by broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum buds from a narrow base and has a thinner cell membrane than Blastomyces.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. appear in tissue as aseptate hyphae rather than as budding yeast cells.

questions.stem: Sputum from a 35-year-old man receiving corticosteroids is examined microscopically. Small yeast cells are budding from a narrow base, so that each parent and daughter pair resembles an infinity sign. Which of the following organisms is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Histoplasma capsulatum yeast bud from a narrow base, producing the characteristic infinity-sign appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Histoplasma capsulatum, new yeast cells bud with a narrow base so that the budding pair looks similar to an infinity sign, which is referred to as narrow-based budding. This is the counterpart to the broad-based budding of Blastomyces dermatitidis and is how the two thermally dimorphic yeasts are separated in tissue and sputum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. appear as septate hyphae in specimens rather than as budding yeast cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis buds across a thick, wide base and has a thicker-appearing cell membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans causes endogenous overgrowth syndromes such as thrush and is not defined by narrow-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. appear as aseptate hyphae in specimens rather than as budding yeast cells.

questions.stem: A clinical specimen is plated on agar and grows colonies that resemble bacterial colonies rather than fluffy, velvet-like growth. Microscopy shows individual round cells dividing asymmetrically. Which of the following best describes this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A dimorphic fungus in its mold phase

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mold bearing conidia on aerial hyphae

choices.label: C
choices.text: A mycelium composed of septate hyphae

choices.label: D
choices.text: A yeast that is reproducing by budding

choices.label: E
choices.text: An aseptate mold in its filamentous phase

explanation.summary: Yeasts are single-celled fungi whose agar colonies look like bacterial colonies; budding is asymmetric division, fission is symmetric.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some fungi exist only as yeasts, single-celled fungi that reproduce by budding, which is asymmetric division, or by fission, which is symmetric. On agar plates, yeast colonies look like bacterial colonies. By contrast, molds are multicellular structures of hyphae with attached conidia, and their colonies are fluffy and can look like velvet.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The mold phase of a dimorphic fungus is filamentous and fluffy, not composed of asymmetrically dividing single cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A conidia-bearing mold would form the fluffy, velvet-like colonies described as the alternative here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A septate mycelium is multicellular and filamentous rather than a population of individually budding cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An aseptate mold still grows as filaments and would not produce bacterial-appearing colonies of single cells.

questions.stem: Bacterial cell walls are built primarily of peptidoglycan. The fungal cell wall is composed primarily of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chitin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ergosterol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipopolysaccharide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mannoproteins

choices.label: E
choices.text: β-glucans

explanation.summary: β-glucans are the primary structural polysaccharide of the fungal cell wall, analogous to peptidoglycan in bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungi have a thick cell wall built from several groups of polysaccharides and proteoglycans. Just as bacterial cell walls are primarily formed of peptidoglycan, fungal cell walls are primarily composed of β-glucans, including β-(1,3)-glucan and β-(1,6)-glucan. Because β-glucans are found only in fungi, they are an attractive antifungal drug target.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chitin is a genuine cell wall component, but it contributes rigidity rather than forming the bulk of the wall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ergosterol resides in the fungal cell membrane beneath the wall, not in the wall itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipopolysaccharide is a component of the Gram-negative bacterial outer membrane, not of fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mannoproteins are present in the wall and aid cell integrity, but they are not its primary structural material.

questions.stem: Which of the following components of the fungal cell wall is a structural polysaccharide whose main contribution is added rigidity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chitin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholesterol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ergosterol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lipoteichoic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peptidoglycan

explanation.summary: Chitin is the fungal cell wall polysaccharide that adds rigidity to the wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to the β-glucans that make up the bulk of the fungal cell wall, chitin is another key structural polysaccharide that adds rigidity to the wall. It sits in the layer just outside the phospholipid bilayer of the fungal cell membrane, beneath the glucan and mannoprotein layers.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cholesterol is the sterol of human cell membranes and is not part of the fungal cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ergosterol is a sterol in the fungal cell membrane, not a cell wall polysaccharide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipoteichoic acid is a Gram-positive bacterial cell wall component and is absent from fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peptidoglycan is the primary structural polymer of bacterial cell walls rather than fungal ones.

questions.stem: One component of the fungal cell wall consists of proteins carrying mannose-rich polysaccharide chains. Besides helping maintain cell integrity, these molecules are notable because they do which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Are recognized by the host immune system

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bind amphotericin B before it can reach the membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: Catalyze polymerization of β-glucan chains within the wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Digest keratin in the stratum corneum during invasion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replace ergosterol in membranes of dimorphic fungi

explanation.summary: Mannoproteins support fungal cell integrity and are also recognized by the host immune system.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mannoproteins are proteins bearing mannose-rich polysaccharide chains that sit at the outermost layer of the fungal cell wall. They help with cell integrity, but they can also be recognized by the immune system, which makes them relevant to how the host detects and responds to fungal invasion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Amphotericin B acts by binding ergosterol in the membrane; mannoproteins do not intercept it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: β-glucan polymerization is carried out by β-1,3-glucan synthase, the enzyme targeted by echinocandins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratin digestion is accomplished by dermatophyte keratinases, not by cell wall mannoproteins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ergosterol is the sterol of the fungal membrane in general and is not substituted by wall mannoproteins.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman with disseminated candidiasis is started on caspofungin. This drug exerts its antifungal effect by inhibiting which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chitin cross-linking within the fungal cell wall layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of dietary cholesterol into fungal ergosterol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ergosterol binding at the fungal cell membrane surface

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mannoprotein transport to the outer fungal cell surface

choices.label: E
choices.text: β-1,3-glucan synthase within the fungal cell wall pathway

explanation.summary: Echinocandins such as caspofungin competitively inhibit β-1,3-glucan synthase, blocking β-glucan production.
explanation.whyCorrect: The enzyme β-1,3-glucan synthase is responsible for producing the β-glucans that make up the bulk of the fungal cell wall, so it is a major antifungal target. Echinocandins, the class of antifungals whose names end in the suffix "fungin," competitively inhibit β-1,3-glucan synthase and block β-glucan production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chitin adds rigidity to the wall, but it is not the step blocked by the echinocandin class.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fungi synthesize ergosterol themselves; the enzymes of that pathway are targeted by a different drug class.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Binding ergosterol directly in the membrane is the mechanism of the polyenes such as amphotericin B and nystatin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mannoprotein trafficking to the cell surface is not the target of any antifungal discussed here.

questions.stem: Echinocandins are fungicidal rather than fungistatic. Which of the following best explains how these drugs kill the fungal cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduced β-1,3-glucan leaves the cell unable to resist osmotic stress

choices.label: B
choices.text: They bind ergosterol and create pores that allow ions to leak out

choices.label: C
choices.text: They block nuclear fusion and prevent the zygote from forming

choices.label: D
choices.text: They inhibit the fungal ribosome and halt all new protein synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: They strip mannoproteins and expose the cell to complement lysis

explanation.summary: Blocking β-glucan production leaves the fungal cell osmotically fragile, so it lyses and dies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Echinocandins are fungicidal, meaning they kill fungi rather than merely halting growth. Decreased production of β-1,3-glucan weakens the cell wall so that the fungal cell faces overwhelming osmotic stress, which results in cell lysis and death. This is a direct consequence of competitively inhibiting β-1,3-glucan synthase.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Binding ergosterol and creating membrane holes is how the polyenes amphotericin B and nystatin act.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blocking karyogamy would interfere with sexual reproduction but is not an antifungal drug mechanism described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Echinocandins act on the cell wall synthesis pathway rather than on fungal ribosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Echinocandins do not remove mannoproteins; their target is the enzyme that builds β-glucans.

questions.stem: Human cell membranes contain cholesterol to support the ion transport channels that line the membrane. The corresponding sterol found in the fungal cell membrane is which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chitin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholesterol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ergosterol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lipoteichoic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: β-(1,6)-glucan

explanation.summary: Fungal membranes contain ergosterol where human membranes contain cholesterol, which is why ergosterol is a selective drug target.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fungal cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer lying beneath the cell wall, and like our own membranes it contains a sterol that supports the ion transport channels within it. Human cells use cholesterol, whereas fungal cells use ergosterol. Because ergosterol is absent from our cells, several antifungal drugs target it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chitin is a rigid polysaccharide of the fungal cell wall rather than a membrane sterol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cholesterol is the human membrane sterol; with the exception of Mycoplasma, bacteria have no membrane sterols at all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipoteichoic acid is a Gram-positive bacterial cell wall component and is not present in fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.E: β-(1,6)-glucan is a cell wall polysaccharide and is not a sterol within the membrane.

questions.stem: Amphotericin B and nystatin belong to the polyene class of antifungals. Which of the following best describes how these drugs damage the fungal cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They bind ergosterol and create holes that let ions leak out

choices.label: B
choices.text: They block fusion of nuclei during sexual reproduction

choices.label: C
choices.text: They chelate mannose residues on the fungal cell surface

choices.label: D
choices.text: They competitively inhibit the enzyme that produces β-glucans

choices.label: E
choices.text: They prevent conidia from germinating into new mycelia

explanation.summary: Polyenes bind ergosterol in the fungal membrane, creating holes through which ions leak until the fungus dies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several drugs used to treat fungal infection target ergosterol because it is absent from human cells. Polyenes, such as amphotericin B and nystatin, bind directly to ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane. This binding creates holes in the membrane and causes ions to leak out of the cell, which leads to death of the fungus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Interfering with karyogamy is not how polyenes exert their antifungal effect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Polyenes act on the membrane sterol, not by chelating surface mannose residues.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Competitive inhibition of β-1,3-glucan synthase is the mechanism of the echinocandin class.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preventing germination of conidia is not the described mechanism of any antifungal class here.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man receiving intravenous amphotericin B for an invasive fungal infection is found to have a serum potassium concentration of 2.8 mEq/L. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds potassium within the gut lumen and blocks its absorption

choices.label: B
choices.text: It causes vomiting severe enough to deplete total body potassium stores

choices.label: C
choices.text: It drives potassium into cells by stimulating the Na+/K+-ATPase pump

choices.label: D
choices.text: It inhibits aldosterone release from the adrenal cortex, wasting potassium

choices.label: E
choices.text: It perforates the renal collecting duct, letting potassium leak into urine

explanation.summary: Amphotericin B perforates the renal tubular collecting duct because human sterols resemble fungal ones, causing urinary potassium loss.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because of the similarity between the sterols in the fungal cell membrane and those in our own cell membranes, amphotericin B perforates the renal tubular collecting duct. This causes potassium to leak out into the urine and can produce a precipitous drop in serum potassium, so electrolytes must be monitored during therapy. The drug is also known for the "shake-and-bake" fever and chills that accompany infusion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amphotericin B is given intravenously for invasive disease and does not act as a gut potassium binder.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gastrointestinal losses do not account for this effect; the renal collecting duct is the site of injury.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transcellular potassium shifting is not the described mechanism; potassium is actually lost from the body in urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The hypokalemia comes from direct renal tubular injury by the drug, not from suppressed aldosterone signaling.

questions.stem: Which of the following categories accounts for the most common type of fungal infection in humans?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infections acquired only by direct person-to-person contact

choices.label: B
choices.text: Infections limited to patients with inherited complement deficiency

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infections restricted to the hair shafts and the nail beds

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunistic infections by ubiquitous fungi or normal microbiota

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic infections caused by dimorphic saprophytic soil fungi

explanation.summary: Opportunistic infections are the most common type of fungal infection, caused by ubiquitous organisms or members of our own microbiota.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pathogenic fungi cause superficial, opportunistic, or systemic infections. Opportunistic fungal infections are the most common of the three. Opportunistic fungal pathogens are typically ubiquitous in the environment or part of our own microbiota, and they cause severe systemic illness in the immunosuppressed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Person-to-person spread is not how the opportunistic category is defined; these organisms are ubiquitous or endogenous.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Opportunistic fungal infection is tied to immunosuppression broadly, not to inherited complement deficiency specifically.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Superficial infections of hair and nails are common but are a distinct, third category from the opportunistic infections.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Systemic mycoses from dimorphic saprophytic fungi are an important category but are not the most common one.

questions.stem: A previously healthy 29-year-old park ranger with no known immunodeficiency develops a systemic fungal illness after prolonged work in freshly disturbed soil. Which of the following statements best characterizes this class of fungal infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Systemic mycoses arise from overgrowth of the patient's own resident normal flora

choices.label: B
choices.text: Systemic mycoses come from dimorphic saprophytic fungi and can sicken healthy hosts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Systemic mycoses occur only after a breach of the skin or a mucosal barrier

choices.label: D
choices.text: Systemic mycoses remain confined to the stratum corneum, the hair, and nails

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic mycoses require an absolute neutrophil count below 500 cells per µL

explanation.summary: Systemic fungal infections are usually caused by dimorphic saprophytic fungi, and exposure to their conidia can cause illness even in immunocompetent people.
explanation.whyCorrect: Systemic fungal infections are usually caused by dimorphic saprophytic fungi. What distinguishes them from the opportunistic infections is that exposure to a sufficient burden of conidia can cause illness even in immunocompetent people. These fungi live in soil as mycelium, and inhaled spores convert to yeast within tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Overgrowth of resident flora describes endogenous infection such as thrush, not the systemic mycoses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Systemic mycoses typically begin with inhalation of conidia rather than requiring a break in the skin or mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Confinement to keratinized surfaces describes superficial infection, the opposite of a systemic mycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immunosuppression worsens these infections but is not a requirement, since healthy people can also become ill.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy has several expanding annular scaly plaques on his trunk. The responsible organisms adhere to keratinocytes, germinate, and produce keratinases. Which of the following best describes these fungi?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aseptate molds that invade blood vessels in diabetic patients

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dermatophytes that infect the stratum corneum, hair shafts, and nails

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encapsulated yeasts that disseminate to the central nervous system

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunistic yeasts derived from the patient's own oral microbiota

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thermally dimorphic fungi acquired by inhaling airborne soil conidia

explanation.summary: Dermatophytes infect keratinized structures, producing keratinases to feed on keratin and causing ringworm, jock itch, and nail infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dermatophytes infect the stratum corneum, hair shafts, and nails. Their spores adhere to keratinocytes, germinate, and produce keratinases, which also promote more avid adherence of the fungi. They feed on the keratin of skin and nails and spread to cause common infections such as jock itch, ringworm (tinea corporis), and nail infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aseptate angioinvasive molds cause severe invasive disease in the immunocompromised rather than superficial ringworm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An encapsulated yeast disseminating to the nervous system describes a systemic infection, not a dermatophyte.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral microbiota overgrowth produces endogenous disease such as thrush, not annular scaly plaques on the trunk.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thermally dimorphic fungi are inhaled and cause pulmonary or systemic disease, not keratin-restricted plaques.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman develops white plaques on her buccal mucosa. Cultures grow a fungus that is a normal inhabitant of the oral cavity. This infection is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A superficial dermatophyte infection of a keratinized surface

choices.label: B
choices.text: A systemic mycosis caused by a thermally dimorphic organism

choices.label: C
choices.text: A zoonotic infection transmitted by contact with bird droppings

choices.label: D
choices.text: An endogenous infection from overgrowth of normal flora

choices.label: E
choices.text: An exogenous infection acquired by inhaling conidia from soil

explanation.summary: Thrush is an endogenous infection: Candida is already part of normal flora and simply overgrows.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungal infections are either exogenous or endogenous, a distinction that refers to whether the fungus is normally part of our flora. Endogenous infections are caused by proliferation of our own normal flora, and thrush is the classic example: overgrowth of Candida spp. causes a white plaque to form in the mouth, which in severe cases can spread down the esophagus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dermatophytes infect the stratum corneum, hair, and nails rather than the moist buccal mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A systemic mycosis from a thermally dimorphic fungus is an exogenous, usually inhaled, infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bird-dropping exposure is an epidemiologic clue for an exogenous soil fungus, not for oral candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Exogenous infection involves fungi not normally found in our flora, such as soil organisms whose conidia are inhaled.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with asthma who has been using an inhaled corticosteroid develops white plaques in her mouth. Which of the following best explains her susceptibility to this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The steroid acts as a direct growth factor for Candida in the oropharynx

choices.label: B
choices.text: The steroid destroys the mucosal barrier by dissolving keratinocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: The steroid inhibits NF-κB, producing local immunosuppression in the mouth

choices.label: D
choices.text: The steroid raises oral pH and drives Candida into its hyphal form

choices.label: E
choices.text: The steroid selectively kills oral bacteria and allows Candida to expand

explanation.summary: Inhaled corticosteroids inhibit NF-κB and cause local immunosuppression, letting resident oral Candida overgrow into thrush.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients taking inhaled corticosteroids for asthma are prone to thrush, a localized oral Candida infection. Corticosteroids inhibit the transcription factor NF-κB, which causes local immunosuppression in the mouth. Candida is naturally present there, so without immune regulation of its growth the fungus is allowed to flourish.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corticosteroids do not serve as a nutrient or growth factor for Candida.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mucosal barrier is not dissolved; the defect is in immune regulation of resident fungal growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Candida form is influenced by pH and nutrients, but the reason for thrush here is blunted local immunity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The predisposing problem is local immunosuppression from the steroid, not direct killing of oral bacteria.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man from Ohio develops fever, cough, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates several weeks after clearing out an attic heavily soiled with bat droppings. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucor spp.

explanation.summary: Histoplasma is endemic to the Ohio and Mississippi river valleys and is acquired by inhaling conidia from soil contaminated with bird or bat droppings.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma spp. are found in the central and eastern United States, especially in the Ohio and Mississippi river valleys. Transmission occurs by inhalation of conidia, usually from soil contaminated with bird or bat droppings. Most people are asymptomatic or have moderate flu-like symptoms, but pneumonia with potential systemic dissemination can occur, particularly in the immunocompromised.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. are ubiquitous opportunists and are not tied to river-valley endemicity or bat guano exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis is a thermally dimorphic fungus but lacks the bird and bat dropping exposure link described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans causes endogenous disease from normal flora overgrowth rather than inhalational exposure from soil.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. are opportunists causing severe disease in the immunocompromised, without this geographic and exposure profile.

questions.stem: A patient with a suspected invasive fungal infection has specimens sent for several laboratory tests. Which of the following methods provides species-level identification and enables antifungal susceptibility testing, but may require days to weeks for a result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen detection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct microscopy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histopathology

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serology

explanation.summary: Culture is the general gold standard because it identifies the species and permits susceptibility testing, at the cost of a slow turnaround.
explanation.whyCorrect: Culture is generally considered the gold standard for diagnosis of fungal infection because it provides species-level identification and enables antifungal susceptibility testing. Its drawbacks are that it often requires days to weeks for results and may have limited sensitivity for certain infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antigen detection identifies fungal polysaccharides or proteins in tissue but does not produce an isolate for testing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct microscopy visually inspects the size and shape of the fungus and does not yield a susceptibility profile.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histopathology looks for histological markers of fungus in tissue rather than growing the organism for identification.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is used to quickly determine whether IgM or IgG has been generated, not to identify a species for susceptibility testing.

questions.stem: A diagnostic assay is used to rapidly determine whether a patient has produced IgM or IgG during an immune response to a fungus. This method is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen detection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct microscopy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histopathology

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serology

explanation.summary: Serology detects host antibody (IgM or IgG) generated in response to a fungus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serology is used to quickly determine the presence of immunoglobulin M (IgM) or IgG that has been generated during an immune response to a fungus. It measures the host response rather than the organism itself, which is what separates it from the direct detection methods.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antigen detection uses antibodies to find fungal antigens in the patient, which is the reverse of measuring host antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Culture grows the organism for species identification and susceptibility testing rather than measuring antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct microscopy inspects the size and shape of the fungus itself and reports no immunoglobulin data.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histopathology checks tissue for histological markers that highlight the presence of a fungus.

questions.stem: A laboratory assay uses antibodies directed against specific fungal polysaccharides and proteins that may be present in a patient's tissues during infection. This method is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen detection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct microscopy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histopathology

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serology

explanation.summary: Antigen detection uses antibodies aimed at fungal polysaccharides or proteins to identify the responsible fungus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antigen detection uses antibodies that are directed at various specific fungal polysaccharides or proteins that can be present in tissues during the course of an infection. These antibodies complex with the specific antigens if they are present, which aids in identifying the type of fungus responsible for the infection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Culture requires growing the organism and is the slow but definitive route to species identification.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct microscopy relies on visual inspection of fungal size and shape without any antibody reagent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histopathology looks for histological markers of fungus in tissue sections rather than using directed antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology measures the patient's own IgM or IgG rather than detecting fungal antigen in tissue.

questions.stem: A technologist needs a routine stain to visualize the conidia and hyphae of a mold growing on a culture plate. Which of the following is a common stain used for fungi?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Congo red stain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giemsa stain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lactophenol blue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast stain

explanation.summary: Lactophenol blue is a common stain used to visualize fungal structures such as conidia and hyphae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lactophenol blue is a common stain for fungi and is used to display structures such as the microconidia and macroconidia that distinguish one mold from another. Fungal elements in tissue can also be shown with periodic acid-Schiff and Grocott-Gomori methenamine-silver stains.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congo red is used to demonstrate amyloid deposits in tissue rather than fungal structures.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Giemsa stain is applied to blood films and is not the routine stain for mold morphology on plates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Gram stain is designed to separate bacteria by cell wall type rather than to display fungal conidia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast stain is used for mycobacteria and related acid-fast organisms.

questions.stem: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that bacteria failed to grow around a contaminant on one of his Staphylococcus aureus plates, and the chemical responsible was later named after that contaminating organism. The contaminant belonged to which of the following groups?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fungus of the genus Penicillium

choices.label: B
choices.text: A Gram-positive spore-forming bacterium

choices.label: C
choices.text: A mycobacterial species from laboratory air

choices.label: D
choices.text: A protozoan carried on the culture loop

choices.label: E
choices.text: A thermally dimorphic soil yeast

explanation.summary: Penicillin was discovered from a Penicillium mold contaminating a staphylococcal plate, and the drug was named after the fungus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fleming accidentally discovered penicillin after noticing that one of his petri dishes of S. aureus had been contaminated with a fungus, and that the bacteria did not grow around it. The chemical that blocked bacterial growth was named penicillin after that fungus, Penicillium notatum. Florey and Chain later purified penicillin and demonstrated its use in animal infections, and by the late 1940s it was in mass production.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The contaminant was a fungus, not a spore-forming bacterium; the bacterium on the plate was S. aureus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mycobacteria are acid-fast bacteria and had no role in this discovery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The zone of inhibition was produced by a mold, not by a protozoan contaminant.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thermally dimorphic soil fungi are human pathogens such as Histoplasma, not the source of penicillin.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man completes a 10-day course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic for pneumonia. He now reports a sore mouth and a change in taste. Examination shows curd-like white patches on the buccal mucosa and tongue that are easily removed with moderate scraping, leaving an erythematous base. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus fumigatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epstein-Barr virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Thrush is an overgrowth of Candida spp. in the mouth, most often after antibiotic use or during immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida spp. are normal flora of the mouth and throat, and disruption of the normal flora by a broad-spectrum antibiotic allows them to overgrow. Thrush presents as curd-like white patches that are easily removed with moderate scraping. C. albicans is the species responsible for most cases of candidiasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. exist only as molds and cause lung and sinus disease; they do not produce removable oral plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epstein-Barr virus causes hairy cell leukoplakia, whose white patches do not come off with scraping.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. aureus can coinfect angular cheilitis at the corners of the mouth, but it does not cause curd-like removable plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pyogenes is listed as a cause of cheilitis and diaper rash, not of scrapable white plaques on the tongue.

questions.stem: A student is reviewing the organisms that make up the normal human flora. In healthy people, Candida spp. pose little threat and are recovered as commensals from several body sites. Candida spp. primarily colonize which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bladder, ureters, and kidneys

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bloodstream, liver, and spleen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mouth, throat, gut, and vagina

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sinuses, middle ear, and lower airways

choices.label: E
choices.text: Soil, decaying plants, and air

explanation.summary: Candida spp. are human normal flora of the mouth, throat, gastrointestinal tract, and vagina.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida spp. live in harmony with most people as normal flora at these mucosal sites. Disease follows immunosuppression or disruption of the normal flora, often from antibiotic use, which allows overgrowth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The urinary tract is not a normal Candida reservoir; Candida cystitis is a hospital-acquired infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood, liver, and spleen are sterile; Candida spp. reaching the bloodstream represents invasive disease, not colonization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The sinuses and lower airways are sites Aspergillus spp. can colonize; Candida spp. are not normal flora there.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Soil, decaying vegetation, and air are the environmental reservoirs of Aspergillus spp., not of Candida spp.

questions.stem: A hospital laboratory tabulates every Candida isolate recovered from clinical specimens over one year. A single species accounts for roughly 57 percent of the isolates and is responsible for most cases of candidiasis. Which of the following species is it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candida glabrata

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida krusei

choices.label: D
choices.text: Candida parapsilosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Candida tropicalis

explanation.summary: C. albicans is the single most commonly isolated Candida species and causes the most cases of candidiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among Candida species isolated in the clinic, C. albicans accounts for about 57 percent, far more than any other species. The remaining isolates are divided among glabrata, parapsilosis, krusei, and tropicalis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: C. glabrata is second at roughly 17 percent of clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: C. krusei accounts for roughly 5 percent of clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.D: C. parapsilosis accounts for roughly 8 percent of clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. tropicalis accounts for roughly 5 percent of clinical isolates.

questions.stem: The same laboratory reports that, after the single most common species, one other species accounts for about 17 percent of clinical Candida isolates, roughly twice the share of the next species on the list. Which species accounts for that 17 percent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida auris

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candida glabrata

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida krusei

choices.label: D
choices.text: Candida parapsilosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Candida tropicalis

explanation.summary: C. glabrata is the second most frequently isolated Candida species in the clinic at about 17 percent.
explanation.whyCorrect: The relative frequency list runs C. albicans 57 percent, C. glabrata 17 percent, C. parapsilosis 8 percent, then C. krusei and C. tropicalis at 5 percent each. C. glabrata's 17 percent is about twice the 8 percent of C. parapsilosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. auris is rarely seen in the United States and does not appear among the common clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: C. krusei accounts for roughly 5 percent, not 17 percent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: C. parapsilosis accounts for roughly 8 percent, the species just below the correct answer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. tropicalis accounts for roughly 5 percent, tied with C. krusei.

questions.stem: A hospital epidemiologist reviews susceptibility data on Candida auris isolates recovered from intensive care unit patients. Most of the isolates are resistant to fluconazole. Approximately what proportion of C. auris isolates is also resistant to amphotericin B?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fewer than 1 percent

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 3 to 5 percent

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 13 to 35 percent

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 50 to 60 percent

choices.label: E
choices.text: More than 90 percent

explanation.summary: C. auris is commonly multidrug resistant: most isolates resist fluconazole and 13 to 35 percent resist amphotericin B.
explanation.whyCorrect: Between 13 and 35 percent of C. auris isolates are resistant to amphotericin B. Most isolates remain susceptible to the echinocandins, although the minimal inhibitory concentration needed is higher than for C. albicans. Combined with the poor health of the patients it infects, this resistance drives a 30 to 72 percent mortality for hospital-acquired C. auris infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This understates the resistance; amphotericin B resistance in C. auris is common, not exceptional.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is far below the reported range for amphotericin B resistance in this species.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Resistance is substantial but does not reach a majority of isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Near-universal resistance describes fluconazole in this species, not amphotericin B.

questions.stem: An immunocompromised man has white patches on the lateral tongue and buccal mucosa. His physician wants to distinguish oropharyngeal candidiasis from hairy cell leukoplakia at the bedside. Which of the following findings would best support a diagnosis of thrush?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The patches are confined to the lateral border of the tongue

choices.label: B
choices.text: The patches are easily removed with gentle scraping

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patches have been present for many months

choices.label: D
choices.text: The patient also has painful vesicles on the lower lip

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient reports no recent exposure to antibiotics

explanation.summary: Thrush wipes off with gentle scraping; hairy cell leukoplakia does not.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both thrush and hairy cell leukoplakia present as white oral patches in immunocompromised patients, so they look alike. The quick bedside discriminator is scraping: the curd-like plaques of thrush come off, while the lesions of hairy cell leukoplakia, which is caused by Epstein-Barr virus, remain adherent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Location does not separate the two, and both may involve the tongue and adjacent mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Duration does not discriminate; both occur in immunocompromised patients and may persist.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lip vesicles are a separate finding and do not distinguish these two white-patch diseases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiotic exposure raises suspicion for thrush, but its absence does not exclude it, since immunosuppression and oral trauma also cause it.

questions.stem: An 81-year-old nursing home resident with no recent antibiotic use and no known immunodeficiency develops white plaques on the gums and palate. Her dentures were fitted many years ago and now slip and rub against her gums when she chews. Which of the following best explains why she developed this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhaled spores colonized a pre-existing mucosal cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of normal flora from a broad-spectrum antibiotic course

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeated trauma from the ill-fitting dentures damaged her gums

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rising estrogen levels changed her mucosal environment

choices.label: E
choices.text: The infection spread person-to-person from another resident

explanation.summary: Oral trauma, classically from poorly fitting dentures, is a third route to thrush besides antibiotics and immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thrush most commonly follows antibiotic use or immunosuppression, but oral trauma can also cause it. Poorly fitting dentures rub against and damage the gums, which can lead to infection by Candida spp. or by the other bacteria in the mouth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colonization of a pre-existing cavity by inhaled spores describes aspergilloma in the lung, not thrush.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The stem specifies that she has had no recent antibiotic exposure, so loss of flora from antibiotics cannot explain it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased estrogen is a risk factor for vulvovaginal candidiasis, not for oral thrush.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida spp. cause disease by overgrowth of the patient's own normal flora, not by person-to-person spread.

questions.stem: A man with severe immunosuppression is being treated for thrush. He now reports retrosternal chest discomfort and pain with swallowing, and his oral infection is presumed to have extended beyond the mouth. Which of the following complications has most likely developed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balanitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endocarditis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Esophagitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meningitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyelonephritis

explanation.summary: In severe immunosuppression, thrush can spread beyond the mouth to the pharynx and esophagus, producing Candida esophagitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Esophagitis is one of the five superficial Candida infections and is the direct downstream extension of thrush. Patients with severe immunosuppression are the ones in whom the infection spreads past the oropharynx.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balanitis is a superficial infection of the penis and is unrelated to extension of oral disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida endocarditis follows hematogenous dissemination, not contiguous spread from the mouth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Candida meningitis is a manifestation of disseminated invasive disease in severely ill patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyelonephritis arises from an ascending urinary tract infection, not from oral thrush.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman presents with vulvar itching and a thick, white, curd-like vaginal discharge. She has taken no antibiotics recently, has no history of diabetes, and is not immunosuppressed. Which element of her history is the most likely predisposing factor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She eats a diet that is high in refined sugars

choices.label: B
choices.text: She exercises at a gym three times every week

choices.label: C
choices.text: She recently began combined oral contraceptives

choices.label: D
choices.text: She recently traveled to a hot and humid climate

choices.label: E
choices.text: She uses only unscented laundry soap at home

explanation.summary: Increased estrogen levels, including from birth control, raise the risk of vulvovaginal candidiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Risk factors for yeast infections are antibiotic use, increased estrogen levels from pregnancy, birth control, or hormone therapy, diabetes, immunosuppression, and anything that alters vaginal pH. The stem excludes antibiotics, diabetes, and immunosuppression, leaving the estrogen exposure from her oral contraceptive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dietary sugar is not among the listed risk factors for vulvovaginal candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Routine exercise is not one of the identified predisposing factors for this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heat and humidity predispose to Candida intertrigo in skin folds, not to vulvovaginal candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Using unscented soap does not alter vaginal pH and is not a risk factor.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old uncircumcised man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes reports several days of burning, tenderness, and itching of the glans and foreskin. Examination shows inflammation with a curd-like exudate beneath the foreskin. Which of the following most likely contributed to his infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A recent course of corticosteroids for an asthma flare

choices.label: B
choices.text: A recent surgical procedure on the genitourinary tract

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure to clean adequately beneath the foreskin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior instrumentation of the urethra with a catheter

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recent sexual contact with a partner who has urethritis

explanation.summary: Candida balanitis is favored by diabetes, obesity, immunosuppression, and being uncircumcised with inadequate hygiene under the foreskin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Failure to clean properly underneath the foreskin leads to overgrowth of normal flora and potentially to infection. Candida balanitis presents with pain, tenderness, burning, and pruritus of the foreskin or penis developing over several days, often with a curd-like or purulent exudate. Having a partner with a vulvovaginal yeast infection also increases risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corticosteroids are a listed risk for invasive Aspergillus disease, not a described cause of balanitis here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Recent surgery is a risk factor for invasive candidiasis, not for this superficial infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urethral catheters predispose to urinary tract infection, not to inflammation of the glans and foreskin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A partner with vulvovaginal candidiasis raises risk, but urethritis in a partner is not a listed risk factor for Candida balanitis.

questions.stem: An obese 45-year-old woman has a rash beneath both breasts. The involved skin is red, moist, and shiny, described as beefy in appearance, and several small pustules sit just beyond the border of the main rash. Which combination of local factors best explains this presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cold air, wind exposure, and chronic scratching

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contact with detergents, dyes, and added fragrances

choices.label: C
choices.text: Friction, moisture, and heat within the skin folds

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sun exposure, dryness, and repeated shaving of the area

choices.label: E
choices.text: Venous stasis, dependent edema, and poor arterial flow

explanation.summary: Candida intertrigo is inflammation of the skin folds driven by friction, moisture, and heat, with beefy red skin and satellite pustules.
explanation.whyCorrect: Superficial Candida skin infections are often classified as intertrigo, inflammation of the skin folds, and are associated with friction, moisture, and heat. The presentation is described as beefy because the skin is red, moist, and shiny like raw beef, and satellite pustules may be present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cold and wind do not create the warm, damp fold environment in which Candida spp. overgrow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Detergents and fragrances produce contact dermatitis, which is not the Candida skin infection described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sun exposure and dryness are the opposite of the moist, occluded environment that favors intertrigo.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Venous stasis and arterial insufficiency cause lower leg skin changes, not fold infection with satellite pustules.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old infant who is finishing a course of amoxicillin for otitis media and recovering from several days of diarrhea develops a rash in the diaper area. The rash consists of beefy red plaques, papules, and pustules that scale when they rupture, and the skin folds are the worst affected. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus fumigatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epstein-Barr virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Diaper rash is often caused by Candida spp., especially after diarrhea, infrequent diaper changes, or recent antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida diaper rash presents as beefy red plaques, papules, and pustules that scale when ruptured, with the skin folds most severely involved. A recent history of diarrhea, infrequent diaper changes, or recent antibiotic use are the commonly associated exposures, and this infant has two of the three.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. are environmental molds causing lung and sinus disease, not diaper dermatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epstein-Barr virus causes hairy cell leukoplakia in the mouth, not a diaper-area rash.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. saprophyticus is a cause of urinary tract infection, not of diaper dermatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pyogenes can cause diaper rash and cheilitis, but the beefy fold-predominant rash following antibiotics and diarrhea points to Candida.

questions.stem: A patient being treated for thrush develops inflammation, ulceration, and crusted fissures at both corners of the mouth. A swab grows Candida albicans together with a second organism. Besides Candida spp., which of the following most commonly causes or coinfects this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus fumigatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epstein-Barr virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: Angular cheilitis can be caused by Candida spp. alone or coinfected with bacteria such as S. aureus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Angular cheilitis is inflammation at the corners of the mouth that leads to ulceration and crusted fissures. It may arise on its own or as a complication of thrush, and bacterial coinfection is common, classically with S. aureus. Candida-bacterial coinfection of these lesions is explicitly described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. are inhaled environmental molds and are not described as coinfecting cheilitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus causes hairy cell leukoplakia, a separate oral white-patch disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: E. coli is a common cause of urinary tract infection, not of angular cheilitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. saprophyticus is a urinary pathogen and is not implicated in lesions at the mouth corners.

questions.stem: Four patients are admitted to the hospital on the same day. Which of the following patients is at the highest risk of developing invasive candidiasis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A critically ill man with a central line on broad-spectrum antibiotics

choices.label: B
choices.text: A farmer admitted for an acute exacerbation of his known asthma

choices.label: C
choices.text: A healthy college student admitted overnight after a concussion

choices.label: D
choices.text: A pregnant woman being treated as an outpatient for oral thrush

choices.label: E
choices.text: A teenager admitted for a closed fracture of the left forearm

explanation.summary: Invasive candidiasis strikes immunosuppressed and critically ill patients, especially those with central venous catheters, broad-spectrum antibiotics, or recent surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: The listed risk factors are immunosuppression, critical illness, a central venous catheter, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and recent surgery, and patients who develop invasive candidiasis usually check several of these boxes. A critically ill patient with a central line on broad-spectrum antibiotics checks three. Patients with increased risk factors who are on broad-spectrum antibiotics are at the highest risk.

whyWrongByChoice.B: An asthma exacerbation in a farmer raises concern for Aspergillus-related lung disease, not invasive candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A healthy patient observed after minor head trauma has none of the listed risk factors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thrush treated as an outpatient is a superficial infection and does not itself confer invasive risk.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A closed fracture involves no surgery, no line, and no immunosuppression.

questions.stem: Candida spp. are frequent causes of hospital-acquired infection, and some of these infections are life-threatening. Which of the following is the most common invasive disease caused by Candida spp.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bloodstream infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endocarditis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Meningitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pneumonia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyelonephritis

explanation.summary: Candidemia, a bloodstream infection, is the most common invasive disease caused by Candida spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common invasive disease caused by Candida spp. is candidemia. Once dissemination from the bloodstream occurs, infections become extensive and can involve the lungs, heart, central nervous system, and other organ systems.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida endocarditis is a downstream complication of bloodstream infection, not the most common presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida meningitis occurs only after dissemination and is far less common than candidemia itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Candida pneumonia follows dissemination in severely ill patients and is less common than candidemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyelonephritis can seed the bloodstream, but the bloodstream infection is the most common invasive disease.

questions.stem: A woman with severe mucositis and neutropenic colitis after chemotherapy develops candidemia. She has no indwelling intravascular lines and no other identified site of infection. Which of the following best explains how Candida spp. reached her bloodstream?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct inoculation from an intravascular catheter hub

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding from an infected heart valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhalation of conidia circulating in the hospital air

choices.label: D
choices.text: Person-to-person spread from a colonized roommate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Translocation across the gastrointestinal mucosal barrier

explanation.summary: Candida spp. reach the bloodstream by crossing the gastrointestinal mucosal barrier, by an intravascular catheter, or by dissemination from another infected site.
explanation.whyCorrect: There are three predominant routes into the bloodstream: through the gastrointestinal tract mucosal barrier, by an intravascular catheter, and by dissemination from another infection site such as pyelonephritis.
