This patient has no catheter and no other infected site, and her chemotherapy has damaged the gut mucosa where Candida spp. are normal flora, leaving translocation as the route.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The stem states she has no indwelling intravascular lines.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The stem states no other site of infection was identified, so there is no valve source to seed from.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhalation of conidia is how Aspergillus spp. are acquired; Candida spp. do not spread this way.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Candida infections arise from the patient's own flora rather than from person-to-person transmission.

questions.stem: A respiratory specimen from a patient with a suspected fungal infection is stained and examined. The microscopist reports a mixture of budding yeast and hyphae, and several yeast cells show a single early hyphal projection extending from the mother cell. Which organism best fits this description?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus fumigatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aspergillus niger

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blastomyces spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma spp.

explanation.summary: Candida spp. are dimorphic but not thermally dimorphic, so patient samples can contain both yeast and mold forms, and germ tubes are unique to Candida.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because Candida spp. are dimorphic without being thermally dimorphic, both the mold and the yeast form may be present in the same patient sample. The early hyphal outgrowth from a yeast cell is a germ tube, which is a dead giveaway for Candida spp.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. have no single-celled yeast form; only mold is seen in patient samples.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A. niger, like all Aspergillus spp., appears only as mold and does not produce germ tubes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blastomyces spp. are identified by yeast showing broad-based budding, not by germ tubes with hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma spp. are identified by yeast alone in patient samples, without germ tube formation.

questions.stem: A laboratory wishes to confirm that a yeast isolate from a patient is Candida spp. Technicians incubate the yeast in serum at 37 degrees Celsius for 2 to 4 hours and then examine it under the microscope. Which of the following findings would confirm the identification?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Appearance of yeast demonstrating broad-based budding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of the mold into a thermally dimorphic form

choices.label: C
choices.text: Development of black pigmented colonies on the plate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formation of germ tubes from the yeast cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Production of conidiophores bearing conidia

explanation.summary: Growing Candida yeast in serum at 37 degrees Celsius for 2 to 4 hours stimulates germ tube formation, a distinguishing feature of the genus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Germ tubes are an early hyphal growth that emerges from the yeast cell. They can be seen in patient samples and can also be stimulated deliberately in the lab by incubating the yeast in human or animal serum at 37 degrees Celsius for 2 to 4 hours. Their appearance is a dead giveaway for Candida spp.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Broad-based budding yeast identifies Blastomyces spp. and is not what this test demonstrates.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida spp. are dimorphic but specifically not thermally dimorphic, so no temperature-driven conversion occurs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Black colonies describe the culture appearance of A. niger on agar, not a germ tube test result.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidiophores producing conidia are a feature of sporulating Aspergillus spp., not of Candida yeast in serum.

questions.stem: A critically ill patient is strongly suspected of having disseminated candidiasis, yet repeated blood cultures return negative and the team debates whether the diagnosis is still possible. In one study of patients found to have disseminated candidiasis at autopsy, approximately what percentage had positive blood cultures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 10 percent

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 25 percent

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 50 percent

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 75 percent

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 95 percent

explanation.summary: Blood cultures were positive in only about 50 percent of patients with disseminated candidiasis found at autopsy, which is why non-culture tests are also used.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bloodstream infections caused by Candida spp. are difficult to diagnose rapidly. In one study, blood cultures were positive in only approximately 50 percent of patients shown to have disseminated candidiasis at autopsy. Because of this poor yield, both culture and non-culture techniques are used together to identify Candida spp.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This understates the yield of blood culture in disseminated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is below the reported figure; the yield is roughly half, not a quarter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A three-quarters yield would not justify the emphasis on supplementary non-culture testing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Near-complete sensitivity is the opposite of the problem this figure illustrates.

questions.stem: A patient with a suspected invasive fungal infection has a positive beta-D-glucan assay on a serum sample. Which of the following best describes what this result tells the clinician?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms that Candida albicans is the causal organism

choices.label: B
choices.text: It detects a cell wall component unique to Aspergillus spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It identifies which antifungal drugs the isolate will resist

choices.label: D
choices.text: It indicates a fungal infection but not which fungus is present

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reliably distinguishes yeast infections from mold infections

explanation.summary: Beta-D-glucan is a general fungal cell wall marker; it flags fungal infection but cannot name the fungus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The beta-D-glucan assay detects beta-D-glucan, which is present in the cell walls of fungi generally. It therefore cannot tell which fungus is causing the infection and must be paired with identification methods such as culture and staining to confirm a diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The assay is not species specific and cannot single out C. albicans.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Galactomannan is the Aspergillus cell wall component; beta-D-glucan is shared across fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Susceptibility information comes from culture-based testing, not from an antigen assay.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Because the target is common to fungal cell walls, the assay cannot separate yeasts from molds.

questions.stem: A hospital adds an assay that breaks yeast cells apart, copies the released deoxyribonucleic acid, and detects the amplified product using magnetic resonance technology. It can detect as few as 1 to 3 colony-forming units per mL from a blood specimen. Compared with blood culture, what is the principal advantage of this assay?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be run on urine and respiratory specimens

choices.label: B
choices.text: It detects Aspergillus spp. as well as Candida spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It removes the need for any confirmatory testing

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reports antifungal susceptibility at the same time

choices.label: E
choices.text: It returns a result within three to five hours

explanation.summary: The T2Candida assay detects 1 to 3 colony-forming units per mL of blood within three to five hours, far faster than blood culture.
explanation.whyCorrect: T2Candida was approved by the FDA in 2014. It lyses yeast cells, amplifies the target DNA, and detects the amplified DNA by magnetic resonance, producing a result within three to five hours. That speed is what enhances early detection of candidemia relative to culture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The described specimen for this assay is blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a Candida assay; Aspergillus testing uses galactomannan and serum Aspergillus IgG.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both culture and non-culture techniques are used together, so confirmatory testing is still part of the workup.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Culture remains useful precisely because of the risk of antifungal resistance; this assay is not described as giving susceptibility.

questions.stem: A student is comparing the two fungal genera covered in this material and is asked to name a property that separates them. Which of the following is true of Aspergillus spp. but not of Candida spp.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are part of the normal flora of healthy people

choices.label: B
choices.text: They can be grown in the laboratory on Sabouraud agar

choices.label: C
choices.text: They can disseminate to several organs in ill patients

choices.label: D
choices.text: They exist only as a mold and have no yeast form

choices.label: E
choices.text: They stain with periodic acid-Schiff and methenamine silver

explanation.summary: Aspergillus spp. are present only as molds, with no single-celled yeast form, which distinguishes them from Candida spp. in patient samples.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus spp. do not have a single-celled yeast form, so only the mold form appears in patient samples. That helps distinguish Aspergillus spp. from other fungi, including Candida spp., in which both mold and yeast forms may be present together.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is reversed: Candida spp. are normal flora, while Aspergillus spp. are not typically normal flora.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both Candida spp. and Aspergillus spp. can be cultured on Sabouraud agar.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both genera can disseminate to multiple organs in severely ill or immunosuppressed patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PAS and methenamine silver are common fungal stains used for both genera.

questions.stem: Two fungal isolates from different patients are subcultured on Sabouraud agar. The first plate grows bright white, fuzzy colonies. The second plate grows gray colonies with white borders, and a second isolate streaked on that plate is black. Which of the following best identifies the two plates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both plates grew different species within the genus Aspergillus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both plates grew different species within the genus Candida

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither plate grew fungi; both grew bacterial colonies

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plate one grew Aspergillus spp. and plate two grew Candida spp.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plate one grew Candida spp. and plate two grew Aspergillus spp.

explanation.summary: On Sabouraud agar, Candida spp. grow bright white fuzzy colonies while Aspergillus spp. show varied dark or earth-toned pigments.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida spp. cultured on Sabouraud agar appear bright white and fuzzy. Aspergillus spp. have different pigments depending on species: A. fumigatus, the most clinically significant species, appears as gray colonies with white borders, and A. niger colonies are black. The rule to carry is that Candida spp. are white in culture while Aspergillus spp. are usually dark or earth toned.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. do not produce bright white fuzzy colonies like those on the first plate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida spp. do not produce gray and black pigmented colonies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sabouraud agar is used to select for fungi, and both described growths are fungal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the color rule; the bright white fuzzy growth belongs to Candida spp.

questions.stem: A previously healthy landscaper is found to have an Aspergillus infection of the lungs after months of working around decaying plant material. Which of the following is the most common route by which Aspergillus spp. reach a patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contact with an infected animal or its bedding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct person-to-person respiratory spread

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhalation of conidia from the environment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Introduction through an intravascular catheter

choices.label: E
choices.text: Migration of the patient's own normal flora

explanation.summary: Aspergillus spp. are acquired environment-to-person by breathing in conidia, not from the patient's own flora.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus spp. are incredibly common in the environment, found in soil and decaying vegetation, with conidia commonly present in the air, and people breathe in these spores daily. Infection follows when inhaled conidia establish in a susceptible host. A. fumigatus is the most clinically significant species, with A. flavus, A. niger, and A. terreus also causing disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Animal-to-person transmission is an unlikely route for these environmental molds.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Person-to-person spread is an unlikely route of transmission for Aspergillus spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intravascular catheters are a route into the bloodstream for Candida spp., not the usual portal for Aspergillus spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Migration of normal flora is the Candida route; Aspergillus spp. are not typically normal flora.

questions.stem: A transplant service wants to identify the patients at greatest risk for invasive Aspergillus infection so that they can be monitored closely. Which of the following patients is at the highest risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A child finishing a ten-day course of an oral antibiotic

choices.label: B
choices.text: A healthy adult who gardens most weekends in the spring

choices.label: C
choices.text: A leukemia patient with prolonged and severe neutropenia

choices.label: D
choices.text: A middle-aged man with well-controlled essential hypertension

choices.label: E
choices.text: A young woman recovering from a vulvovaginal yeast infection

explanation.summary: Prolonged neutropenia, corticosteroid therapy, transplantation, and HIV/AIDS are the conditions that most raise the risk of invasive Aspergillus disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus spp. pose little threat to immunocompetent patients, but in the immunocompromised they cause severe lung infections that can disseminate. The conditions that increase risk are prolonged neutropenia, corticosteroid therapy, solid organ or bone marrow transplantation, and HIV/AIDS, along with lung diseases such as cancer, COPD, and asthma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotic exposure predisposes to Candida overgrowth, not to invasive aspergillosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Healthy patients do not get invasive Aspergillus infections despite routine environmental exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Controlled hypertension is neither an immunosuppressing condition nor a lung disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A superficial Candida infection does not confer risk for invasive mold disease.

questions.stem: Two patients who work around decaying plant material have lung disease attributed to Aspergillus spp. One is diagnosed with hypersensitivity pneumonitis and the other with allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis. Which of the following distinguishes allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis from hypersensitivity pneumonitis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ABPA occurs only in patients with severe immunosuppression

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis requires a pre-existing cavity

choices.label: C
choices.text: In ABPA the fungus colonizes the lungs and sporulates there

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only ABPA is caused by breathing in spores from the outside

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only hypersensitivity pneumonitis can occur in healthy people

explanation.summary: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis follows inhaled spores, whereas ABPA follows actual colonization of the lungs by Aspergillus spp., which then sporulate in place.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is caused by breathing in spores from the environment. ABPA is caused when Aspergillus spp. colonize the lungs, most often in patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis. Once colonized, the fungus sporulates and consistently floods the lungs with spores, driving inflammation and allergic reactions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ABPA occurs in asthma and cystic fibrosis patients and does not require severe immunosuppression.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A pre-existing cavity is the requirement for aspergilloma, not for hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the mechanisms; inhalation of outside spores describes hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Even healthy patients inhaling Aspergillus spores can develop allergic reactions in the lungs, so this does not separate the two.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis has worsening wheeze and shortness of breath that no longer respond to her usual regimen. She has fever, malaise, and episodes of bronchial obstruction, and she expectorates brownish mucus plugs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis from colonization

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aspergilloma seated within a pre-existing lung cavity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candidemia with dissemination to the lung parenchyma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis progressing over years

choices.label: E
choices.text: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis with vessel invasion

explanation.summary: ABPA commonly complicates asthma and cystic fibrosis and looks like an asthma exacerbation, with fever, malaise, bronchial obstruction, and brownish mucus plugs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Colonization of the lungs by Aspergillus spp. in asthma and cystic fibrosis leads to ABPA. Its symptoms resemble asthma and often present as an exacerbation of it, and in severe cases patients have episodes of bronchial obstruction, fever, malaise, expectoration of brownish mucus plugs, and at times hemoptysis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: An aspergilloma requires a pre-existing lung cavity and presents as a mass with chronic cough and weight loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candidemia occurs in critically ill hospitalized patients with catheters or recent surgery, not in this presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis progresses over months to years with nodules and cavitation, not acute obstruction with mucus plugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis occurs in severely immunosuppressed patients, which this woman is not.

questions.stem: When Aspergillus spp. colonize and sporulate within the airways, the lungs are repeatedly flooded with spores, and the resulting inflammation leads to scarring and fibrosis of the airways over time. Which structure does the fungus produce in order to generate these spores?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding daughter cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conidiophores

choices.label: C
choices.text: Germ tubes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hyphal septations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudohyphae

explanation.summary: Sporulating Aspergillus spp. form conidiophores, the structures that produce the conidia that fly off into the environment and are inhaled.
explanation.whyCorrect: When sporulating, Aspergillus spp. produce conidiophores, which in turn produce conidia, the spores. The conidia fly off into the environment and are breathed in. Within a colonized airway, this continuous spore production plus the inflammation of colonization leads to scarring and fibrosis over time.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding daughter cells are produced by yeast, and Aspergillus spp. have no yeast form.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Germ tubes are an early hyphal outgrowth from Candida yeast cells, not a spore-producing structure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Septations are the cross-walls within Aspergillus hyphae, a morphologic feature rather than a spore-producing organ.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudohyphae are a yeast-related growth form and are not how Aspergillus spp. generate conidia.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic Aspergillus colonization outside the lower airways develops facial pain and nasal congestion. Imaging shows opacification of the affected space, and in severe cases of this condition the space becomes obstructed. Which of the following sites has been colonized?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The middle ear

choices.label: B
choices.text: The paranasal sinuses

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pericardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pleural space

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tracheal lumen

explanation.summary: Besides the lungs, Aspergillus spp. commonly colonize the sinuses, and severe cases cause sinus obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Colonization of the sinuses by Aspergillus spp. may occur, and in severe cases obstruction of the sinuses results. This fits inhaled conidia lodging in an air-filled space continuous with the upper airway and producing facial pain, congestion, and opacification on imaging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Middle ear involvement is not among the described clinical manifestations of Aspergillus spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pericardial disease is not a described site of Aspergillus colonization in this context.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pleural space is not described as a site of Aspergillus colonization and would not cause nasal congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tracheal colonization does not explain facial pain, congestion, and opacification of an air-filled space.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with COPD and a history of pulmonary tuberculosis has had a persistent productive cough, weight loss, and recent hemoptysis over three months. CT shows a mass that sits inside a well-defined cavity. Which feature of his history was required for this lesion to form?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His chronic exposure to inhaled corticosteroid therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: His long-standing airflow obstruction from his COPD

choices.label: C
choices.text: His occupational exposure to decaying plant material

choices.label: D
choices.text: His pre-existing lung cavity left by prior tuberculosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: His previous treatment with broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation.summary: An aspergilloma is a fungus ball that forms when Aspergillus spp. invade a pre-existing lung cavity and grow into a mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients who have cavities in their lungs are at risk for infection by Aspergillus spp., which invade the pre-existing cavity and grow into a mass. Common causes of cavity formation include previous infections, sarcoidosis, and cancer, and tuberculosis or other causes of pneumonia can lead to cavitation. Progression is typically over weeks to months with persistent cough, weight loss, and hemoptysis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corticosteroid therapy raises the risk of invasive disease but does not create the cavity a fungus ball needs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: COPD increases risk for invasive Aspergillus disease but does not itself form the cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Environmental exposure supplies the conidia but is universal; the cavity is what makes this lesion possible.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiotic exposure predisposes to Candida overgrowth and plays no role in fungus ball formation.

questions.stem: A fungus ball is confirmed within a pre-existing pulmonary cavity in a man with a worsening cough and hemoptysis. Which of the following is the appropriate management of this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antifungal therapy alone, continued for several months

choices.label: B
choices.text: Broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy plus close observation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Corticosteroids alone, to suppress the allergic response

choices.label: D
choices.text: Observation alone, because these lesions always resolve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical removal of the fungal ball plus antifungal therapy

explanation.summary: Because an aspergilloma is a mass, treatment requires surgery to remove the fungal ball together with antifungal therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Due to the mass associated with this fungal infection, a combination of surgery to remove the fungal ball and antifungals is required to treat aspergilloma. Drug therapy alone does not clear a mass sitting inside a cavity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antifungals alone are insufficient when a fungal mass occupies a cavity; the mass must be removed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibacterial therapy has no activity against a fungal mass caused by Aspergillus spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corticosteroids target the allergic disease of ABPA, not a structural fungal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fungal balls may be asymptomatic, but they can cause worsening cough, weight loss, and hemoptysis and are not left untreated.

questions.stem: A neutropenic patient with fever, chest pain, and cough has a CT that initially showed nodules surrounded by ground-glass opacities. A repeat scan several weeks later shows that a nodule has cavitated and a crescent of air now lies along its margin. Which of the following does this finding represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fungus ball within a long-standing pulmonary cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: A normal finding in a resolving bacterial pneumonia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Colonization of the airway without any tissue invasion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ground-glass change that is diagnostic of Candida pneumonia

choices.label: E
choices.text: The air-crescent sign of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis

explanation.summary: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis typically shows nodules with surrounding ground-glass opacities, and as it progresses, cavitation with an air-crescent sign can appear.
explanation.whyCorrect: Imaging in invasive pulmonary aspergillosis usually demonstrates nodules with surrounding ground-glass opacities, and as the disease progresses, cavity formation is possible and might demonstrate an air-crescent sign. Imaging alone cannot distinguish IPA from other agents, so diagnosis rests on history, exclusion of other etiologies, radiology, and laboratory identification.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An aspergilloma grows inside a cavity that existed beforehand; here the cavity formed as the disease progressed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These are the described radiographic findings of progressive invasive fungal disease, not of resolving bacterial pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Airway colonization without invasion describes ABPA, not progressive nodules with cavitation in a neutropenic host.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No imaging finding is diagnostic of Candida pneumonia, and ground-glass change is nonspecific.

questions.stem: A man with COPD has had months of cough, hemoptysis, sweats, anorexia, weight loss, and fatigue. Imaging over the past year shows slowly enlarging nodules with cavitation, and his team diagnoses chronic pulmonary aspergillosis. Compared with invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, which of the following best characterizes this form of disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It never spreads beyond the lungs to other organ systems

choices.label: B
choices.text: It occurs only in patients with normal immune function

choices.label: C
choices.text: It progresses over hours to days rather than over weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: It progresses over months to years rather than weeks to months

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires a pre-existing cavity in the lung to develop

explanation.summary: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis progresses over months to years, while invasive pulmonary aspergillosis progresses over weeks to months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several diseases caused by Aspergillus spp. fall under the category of chronic pulmonary aspergillosis. Compared with IPA, which occurs over the course of weeks to months, CPA typically progresses over months to years, with fungal hyphae expanding in the lungs and causing nodules and cavitation. Its symptoms include cough, hemoptysis, shortness of breath, chest pain, sweats, anorexia, weight loss, and fatigue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hematogenous spread may occur as CPA worsens, so extrapulmonary disease is possible.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CPA occurs in patients with pre-existing lung disease and can progress to more aggressive disease if immunosuppression continues.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither form moves this quickly; even IPA unfolds over weeks to months.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A pre-existing cavity is required for an aspergilloma, not for chronic pulmonary aspergillosis in general.

questions.stem: A lung biopsy from a febrile immunocompromised patient is stained and examined. The pathologist reports filamentous structures with visible cross-walls that branch at angles below 45 degrees, and no yeast are seen. Which of the following organisms does this description fit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus fumigatus present in its mold form

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candida albicans growing in its yeast phase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Candida albicans that is forming germ tubes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Candida glabrata demonstrating pseudohyphae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Candida tropicalis after incubation in serum

explanation.summary: Aspergillus hyphae are septate and branch at acute angles, usually below 45 degrees, and only the mold form appears in patient samples.
explanation.whyCorrect: In patient samples, Aspergillus spp. are distinct from other fungi since they exist only as a mold form. The hyphae are septate, meaning they have breaks or cross-walls, and they show acute-angle branching, with the angles usually below 45 degrees. A. fumigatus is the most clinically significant species.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A yeast phase would show single cells with budding, not septate branching hyphae without yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Germ tubes emerge from yeast cells, and the specimen contains no yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The description specifies no yeast are present, which does not fit a Candida specimen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum incubation of Candida yeast stimulates germ tubes, which is not what was seen.

questions.stem: A clinician caring for a patient with suspected aspergillosis orders an antigen detection kit that looks for a cell wall component of Aspergillus spp. in blood and respiratory fluids. Which of the following best describes the value of this test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be used only on tissue obtained by surgical biopsy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has poor sensitivity and is paired with other methods

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is definitive on its own, so no other testing is needed

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reliably identifies which Aspergillus species is present

choices.label: E
choices.text: It turns positive only after the infection has resolved

explanation.summary: Galactomannan antigen kits detect an Aspergillus cell wall component but have poor sensitivity and selectivity, so they are combined with other diagnostics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Galactomannan is a component of the cell wall of Aspergillus spp., and antigen detection kits can find it in patient samples such as blood or respiratory fluids. However, these kits have poor sensitivity and selectivity, so they are often paired with other diagnostic methods such as culture, staining, and serum Aspergillus IgG levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: It is run on patient samples such as blood and respiratory fluids, not only on surgical tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Its poor performance characteristics are exactly why it is not used as a standalone test.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The assay detects a genus-level cell wall component and does not distinguish species.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The kit is used to support diagnosis during active infection, not after resolution.

questions.stem: A patient has clinical and radiographic findings consistent with invasive aspergillosis. The team adds a serum test that has high sensitivity and selectivity specifically in patients with findings like his. Which of the following tests did they most likely order?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A galactomannan antigen detection kit

choices.label: B
choices.text: A KOH preparation of a skin scraping

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum Aspergillus IgG levels

choices.label: D
choices.text: The beta-D-glucan assay on serum

choices.label: E
choices.text: The T2Candida magnetic resonance assay

explanation.summary: Serum Aspergillus IgG levels are typically elevated in invasive Aspergillus infection and perform well when clinical and radiographic findings already fit.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serum Aspergillus IgG levels can be tested and are typically elevated in patients with invasive Aspergillus infections. This test has high sensitivity and selectivity in patients whose clinical and radiographic findings are consistent with invasive aspergillosis, which is exactly the setting described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The galactomannan antigen kit has poor sensitivity and selectivity and must be paired with other methods.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A KOH prep is used to clear debris before staining skin or nail specimens, not to diagnose invasive lung disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Beta-D-glucan indicates a fungal infection generally and cannot say which fungus is responsible.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T2Candida is a rapid blood assay for Candida spp., not for Aspergillus spp.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man presents with fever, cough, and myalgias. Two weeks earlier he explored a limestone cave in southern Ohio that was heavily occupied by bats. A chest radiograph shows patchy infiltrates. Which of the following organisms grows especially well in soil enriched with bat and bird droppings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces gilchristii

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: Histoplasma spp. live in soil and grow especially well where bird or bat droppings enrich it, so spelunkers are a classic at-risk group.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma capsulatum is found predominantly in the Ohio and Mississippi river valleys, and its growth is favored by soil enriched with bird or bat droppings. Cave explorers are specifically at increased risk from exposure to bat droppings. Poultry, construction, and landscaping workers are also at elevated risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces spp. grow in soil but have no association with bat or bird droppings; decomposing leaves and wood favor them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces gilchristii shares the soil habitat of B. dermatitidis and likewise lacks any bat or bird dropping association.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides immitis lives in southwestern desert soil and is not linked to bat guano or to the Ohio river valley.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coccidioides posadasii also occupies southwestern soil and has no association with bat droppings.

questions.stem: A microbiology instructor asks a student to name the geographically defined fungus that does not convert between a mold form and a yeast form with temperature. Which of the following organisms should the student name?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus neoformans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: Histoplasma, Blastomyces, and Coccidioides spp. are thermally dimorphic; Cryptococcus spp. are yeasts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus spp. are not generally considered dimorphic, although a mold form can be produced under special laboratory conditions. They are described as yeasts in both the environment and patient samples. The other three genera follow the rule 'mold in the cold (25 degrees C), yeast in the heat (37 degrees C).'

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis is thermally dimorphic, with a yeast form recovered from patient samples at 37 degrees C.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis is thermally dimorphic, converting from arthroconidia-bearing mold to spherules in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii is also thermally dimorphic and forms spherules in the host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma capsulatum is thermally dimorphic, growing as a mold at 25 degrees C and a yeast at 37 degrees C.

questions.stem: A sputum sample from a patient with suspected histoplasmosis is inoculated onto Sabouraud agar and incubated at 25 degrees C. Which of the following morphologies is most likely to be recovered from this plate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encapsulated yeast with an unstained halo

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mold with branching hyphae and conidia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thick-walled spherules packed with endospores

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yeast packed within host macrophages

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast showing broad-based budding

explanation.summary: Thermally dimorphic fungi grow as molds at the cooler incubation temperature of 25 degrees C.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mnemonic for these fungi is 'mold in the cold (25 degrees C), yeast in the heat (37 degrees C).' When Histoplasma spp. are grown at 25 degrees C, they convert to the mold form with hyphae bearing microconidia and macroconidia. Culture on Sabouraud agar can take weeks but confirms the diagnosis and demonstrates thermal dimorphism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An unstained halo around yeast describes the capsule of Cryptococcus spp., which is not thermally dimorphic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spherules are the tissue form of Coccidioides spp. at body temperature, not a 25 degrees C mold feature.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intracellular yeast within macrophages is the 37 degrees C tissue form of Histoplasma spp., not the culture form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Broad-based budding yeast is the 37 degrees C form of Blastomyces spp., not a 25 degrees C culture morphology.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man with AIDS who lives in Tennessee has 3 weeks of fever, weight loss, and pancytopenia. A bone marrow aspirate stained with a fungal stain shows numerous 2 to 5 micrometer yeasts with narrow-based budding, many of them inside macrophages. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus gattii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: Tiny narrow-based budding yeasts sitting inside macrophages are characteristic of Histoplasma spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yeast of Histoplasma spp. are tiny (2 to 5 micrometers) with narrow-based budding, which makes dividing cells look like an hourglass or infinity sign. They are frequently seen inside macrophages and other white blood cells because the organism replicates within macrophages, and dissemination to the bone marrow through the reticuloendothelial system is a recognized feature of severe disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis yeasts are larger than Histoplasma yeasts and show broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis also forms spherules filled with endospores rather than budding yeasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii forms large thick-walled spherules in tissue, not small intracellular budding yeasts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus gattii appears as an encapsulated yeast with a wide unstained zone rather than tiny intracellular forms.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old logger from Wisconsin has a 6-week history of cough and several verrucous skin lesions. A wet preparation of sputum shows large yeasts with a thick connection between the parent and daughter cell. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus neoformans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: Large yeasts with broad-based budding plus skin lesions point to Blastomyces spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yeast of Blastomyces spp. are larger than those of Histoplasma spp. and exhibit broad-based budding, meaning the connection between dividing cells is thick. Skin is the most common site of dissemination in blastomycosis, which fits the verrucous lesions, and outdoor work in an endemic area is the classic exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis produces spherules filled with endospores in tissue, not budding yeasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii likewise forms spherules in patient samples rather than budding yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus neoformans yeasts are surrounded by a huge capsule and are not described by broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma yeasts are small with a narrow-based bud, giving an hourglass rather than a thick connection.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman from Tucson, Arizona, has pneumonia that has not improved on azithromycin. A lung biopsy shows a large, round, thick-walled structure packed with small round bodies within the tissue. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces gilchristii

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus neoformans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: Spherules filled with endospores are the tissue form unique to Coccidioides spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: After inhaled arthroconidia convert in the host, Coccidioides spp. form giant thick-walled structures called spherules that fill with endospores. The spherule eventually ruptures, releasing endospores into surrounding tissue, and each endospore can form another spherule. Biopsy revealing spherules is diagnostic for coccidioidomycosis, and southern Arizona is a high-incidence area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis also produces broad-based budding yeast rather than spherules.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces gilchristii produces large broad-based budding yeast, not endospore-filled structures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus neoformans appears as encapsulated yeast with an unstained zone on staining.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma capsulatum appears as tiny narrow-based budding yeast, often inside macrophages.

questions.stem: A mold isolate grown at 25 degrees C from a patient in California's San Joaquin Valley shows hyphae that break up into chains of barrel-shaped cells resembling a bracelet. Which of the following best describes the structures being observed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arthroconidia that break off the mycelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Budding yeast with a thick connecting isthmus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encapsulated yeast with an unstained halo

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endospores released from a ruptured spherule

choices.label: E
choices.text: Macroconidia that resemble giant suns

explanation.summary: Coccidioides spp. make a specialized conidium called an arthroconidium that gives the mold a bracelet-like appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coccidioides spp. have a specialized type of conidia called arthroconidia, which function just like conidia. They break off from the mycelium and allow the fungus to spread, and they give the mold form of Coccidioides spp. a distinct bracelet-like appearance. Inhaled arthroconidia then convert to spherules in the host.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Broad-based budding yeast is the 37 degrees C form of Blastomyces spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An unstained halo around yeast describes the capsule of Cryptococcus spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endospores are released inside host tissue when a spherule ruptures, not on a 25 degrees C mold plate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Macroconidia resembling giant suns belong to the mold form of Histoplasma spp.

questions.stem: A fungal isolate incubated at 25 degrees C produces hyphae bearing both very large, distinctly knobby conidia that look like giant suns and much smaller conidia alongside them. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with this mold morphology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus gattii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: The mold form of Histoplasma spp. has both microconidia and very distinct macroconidia.
explanation.whyCorrect: When Histoplasma spp. are grown at 25 degrees C they convert to the mold form. Histoplasma spp. have microconidia and macroconidia, and the macroconidia are very distinct, looking like giant suns next to the tinier microconidia. This appearance on culture helps identify the organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis molds have conidia but no macroconidia, which is precisely how they are distinguished from Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis molds also produce arthroconidia rather than paired micro- and macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii molds make barrel-shaped arthroconidia in a bracelet pattern, not macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus gattii is a yeast and is not routinely recovered as a conidia-bearing mold.

questions.stem: A laboratory is examining a mold recovered at 25 degrees C from a patient with pneumonia in an area where both Histoplasma spp. and Blastomyces spp. are endemic. Which of the following culture findings best supports Blastomyces spp. over Histoplasma spp.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arthroconidia alternate along the hyphae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conidia are absent and only bare hyphae are seen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conidia are present but macroconidia are absent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macroconidia are present and microconidia are absent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thick-walled spherules are present within the hyphae

explanation.summary: Blastomyces molds have conidia but no macroconidia, and that absence separates them from Histoplasma molds.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mold form of Blastomyces spp. has conidia but no macroconidia. The lack of macroconidia distinguishes Blastomyces spp. from Histoplasma spp., whose mold form carries both microconidia and very distinct macroconidia. Because the geographic ranges of the two genera overlap substantially, this morphologic difference is a practical discriminator.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alternating arthroconidia along hyphae is the bracelet appearance of Coccidioides spp.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces molds do produce conidia, so completely bare hyphae would not support the identification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Macroconidia point toward Histoplasma spp., the organism this finding is meant to exclude.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spherules form in host tissue for Coccidioides spp. and are not a mold culture feature.

questions.stem: A CSF specimen stained with India ink shows round yeast cells each surrounded by a clear, unstained zone against a dark background. Which of the following structures accounts for this unstained zone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A broad-based bud joining daughter cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: A large polysaccharide capsule around the yeast

choices.label: C
choices.text: A layer of hyphae encircling the yeast

choices.label: D
choices.text: A ring of microconidia around each cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: A thick spherule wall enclosing endospores

explanation.summary: The very large capsule of Cryptococcus spp. excludes stain and produces a clear halo around the yeast.
explanation.whyCorrect: A distinct characteristic of Cryptococcus spp. yeast cells is their very large and distinct capsule. When staining, this huge capsule creates an unstained zone around the yeast. India ink is the classic negative stain method for visualizing the thick capsule of these yeasts in CSF, although it has low sensitivity and is no longer commonly used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Broad-based budding describes the shape of Blastomyces yeast division, not an unstained zone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus in CSF is a yeast and is not encircled by hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microconidia belong to the mold form of Histoplasma spp. and are not seen around yeast in CSF.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spherules are the tissue form of Coccidioides spp. and do not produce a clear halo on India ink.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with advanced HIV infection has 2 weeks of headache and confusion. A lumbar puncture is performed and cryptococcosis is suspected. Which of the following is the preferred diagnostic test on this CSF specimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen detection assay on the CSF

choices.label: B
choices.text: Double immunodiffusion antibody assay

choices.label: C
choices.text: India ink negative stain of the CSF

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mucicarmine stain of the CSF sediment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sabouraud agar culture of the CSF

explanation.summary: Antigen detection assays are the preferred diagnostic test for cryptococcosis in CSF or blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several types of antigen detection assays are available to rapidly detect Cryptococcus antigens in CSF or blood, and these antigen detection assays are the preferred diagnostic test. In the brick's case, antigen detection assays of the CNS were performed and Cryptococcus neoformans antigen was detected in a patient with HIV and suspected meningitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Double immunodiffusion is an antibody assay used for Coccidioides spp., not the preferred cryptococcal test.
whyWrongByChoice.C: India ink is the classic capsule stain but has low sensitivity and is no longer commonly used.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucicarmine highlights the capsule in red but is used particularly in tissue sections rather than as the preferred test.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Culture is the gold standard for diagnosis but is slower than antigen detection and is not the preferred first test.

questions.stem: Which of the following laboratory methods is considered the gold standard for the diagnosis of cryptococcosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Culture of biopsy, sputum, or blood

choices.label: B
choices.text: Double immunodiffusion antibody assay

choices.label: C
choices.text: India ink stain of a CSF sample

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mucicarmine stain of a tissue section

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum antibody titer against the capsule

explanation.summary: Culture remains the gold standard for diagnosing cryptococcosis, even though antigen assays are preferred for speed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Culture is the gold standard for diagnosis of cryptococcosis. Biopsies, sputum, or blood can be grown on Sabouraud or more specialized agars, and on agar the colonies resemble bacterial colonies. Antigen detection assays are still the preferred diagnostic test in practice because they are rapid.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Double immunodiffusion is an antibody assay applied to coccidioidomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: India ink visualizes the capsule but has low sensitivity and is no longer commonly used.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucicarmine stains the polysaccharide capsule red in tissue sections but is not the gold standard.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibody titers are not the described method for confirming cryptococcosis in this brick.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man from Wisconsin with cavitary pneumonia has a culture sent for suspected blastomycosis. The laboratory director notes that culture alone is insufficient and orders a second assay. Which of the following best explains why culture is usually paired with another assay in blastomycosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces spp. cannot grow on Sabouraud agar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture cannot demonstrate thermal dimorphism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Culture cannot distinguish the two Blastomyces species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Culture cross-reacts with Histoplasma antigens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Culture sensitivity is low despite gold standard status

explanation.summary: Culture is the gold standard for blastomycosis but has low sensitivity, so it is paired with another assay.
explanation.whyCorrect: Culture is the gold standard for blastomycosis, but its sensitivity is low, so it is usually paired with another assay such as an antigen detection kit or PCR. PCR can confirm culture or histopathologic identification and can be run on blood to detect disseminated disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces spp. do grow in culture; the limitation is sensitivity rather than an inability to grow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Culture is precisely how thermal dimorphism is demonstrated for these fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Species-level separation of B. dermatitidis and B. gilchristii is not the reason given for pairing assays.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cross-reaction with Histoplasma is a property of antigen detection kits, not of culture.

questions.stem: A urine antigen assay sent to evaluate a patient with suspected histoplasmosis returns positive, and the laboratory notes that this assay can cross-react with Blastomyces antigens. Which of the following best explains why this cross-reactivity is not a major clinical problem?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen assays are always confirmed by India ink stain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces antigens are absent from urine samples

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blastomycosis is confined to the western United States

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blastomycosis resolves without any medical treatment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Both infections are treated with the same antifungals

explanation.summary: Histoplasma antigen tests cross-react with Blastomyces, which matters little because both infections get the same antifungal therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antigen detection kits rapidly identify Histoplasma spp. antigens in serum, urine, sputum, or CNS samples with high sensitivity, non-invasively, and with the quickest turnaround of any test. These antigen tests can cross-react with antigens from Blastomyces, but this is not too problematic since both blastomycosis and histoplasmosis are treated with the same antifungals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: India ink is a cryptococcal capsule stain and is not used to confirm these antigen assays.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces antigens are in fact detectable in urine, which is why urine antigen testing is used.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blastomyces spp. overlap substantially with the Histoplasma range in the central and eastern United States.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Severe blastomycosis in at-risk patients requires treatment and is not assumed to self-resolve.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman develops fever and cough 5 days after cleaning a chicken coop in Missouri. A Histoplasma antibody assay is negative. Which of the following best explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibodies take 2 to 6 weeks to develop after infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibody assays cross-react with Coccidioides only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antibody assays only detect the mold form

choices.label: D
choices.text: Antibody assays require a CSF sample to be valid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Antibody is consumed by circulating fungal antigen

explanation.summary: Anti-Histoplasma antibodies take 2 to 6 weeks to appear, so serology can be falsely negative early in acute infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibodies against Histoplasma spp. typically take between 2 and 6 weeks to develop. This is problematic in acute infections because antibodies may not have developed yet, and in severely immunosuppressed patients titers may never rise sufficiently. For this reason the antibody assay should always be paired with another test.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cross-reaction described in the brick is between Histoplasma and Blastomyces antigen tests, not this scenario.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The antibody assay detects the host immune response and is not restricted to a particular fungal form.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antibody assays are performed on patient serum and do not require CSF.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antigen consumption of antibody is not the explanation the brick gives for early negative serology.

questions.stem: A double immunodiffusion assay is run for suspected coccidioidomycosis. A cloudy line of precipitate forms in the agar between the patient serum well and the central antigen well. Which of the following does this finding indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coccidioides antigen is circulating in the serum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides spherules are present in the serum

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patient has been immunized against Coccidioides

choices.label: D
choices.text: The patient is producing antibodies against Coccidioides

choices.label: E
choices.text: The serum contains no antibody to Coccidioides

explanation.summary: A precipitin line in double immunodiffusion means patient antibody has bound the test antigen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Double immunodiffusion assays are a type of antibody detection assay. Patient samples and Coccidioides antigens are placed in wells in a gel matrix, and the fluids diffuse toward each other. Where antigen and patient sample meet, antibodies and antigens bind and form a cloudy precipitate, so these immune complexes tell you the patient is producing antibodies against Coccidioides antigens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Circulating fungal antigen is measured by a separate antigen assay on urine or serum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spherules are seen on biopsy of tissue, not as a precipitin band in an agar gel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The assay does not distinguish vaccination, and no such immunization is described in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: If the patient were not producing antibodies, the samples would pass by one another and form no precipitate.

questions.stem: A patient in Bakersfield, California, has pneumonia unresponsive to antibiotics, and coccidioidomycosis is suspected. The clinician orders antigen and antibody assays while a culture is still incubating. Which of the following best explains this sequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen assays are required before any culture is set up

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides spp. will not grow on standard agar media

choices.label: C
choices.text: Culture cannot demonstrate the mold form of the fungus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Culture of Coccidioides spp. requires a CSF specimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Culture takes several days, so faster assays are used first

explanation.summary: Coccidioides culture is informative but slow, so rapid antigen and antibody assays are run first.
explanation.whyCorrect: Culture can be used to demonstrate thermal dimorphism at 25 degrees C and the distinct arthroconidia of the mold form of Coccidioides spp. Sabouraud agar can be used to grow the fungi, and they also grow on blood agar. Culture will take several days, so more rapid assays like the antigen and antibody assays are used first.

whyWrongByChoice.A: There is no requirement that antigen testing precede setting up a culture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides spp. grow on Sabouraud agar and on blood agar as well.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Culture at 25 degrees C is exactly how the arthroconidia of the mold form are demonstrated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Respiratory and biopsy specimens are used; CSF is not required to culture this organism.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with recently diagnosed coccidioidomycosis develops painful, red, tender nodules on both shins. Blood cultures and biopsy of a nodule show no fungal organisms. Which of the following best explains these skin findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A drug reaction to the antifungal therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: An immune reaction to circulating fungal antigens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct seeding of the dermis by spherules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hematogenous spread of arthroconidia to the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactivation of a latent cutaneous infection

explanation.summary: Erythema nodosum in the geographically defined mycoses is an immune response to circulating fungal antigen, not dissemination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Immune reactions to fungal antigens circulating in the blood may occur, and the most common is erythema nodosum: painful red nodules on the skin, most commonly on the lower extremities, usually the shins. This is not due to dissemination of the fungi but to the immune system's response to fungal antigens leaking into the blood from the site of infection, which is why the nodules contain no organisms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Erythema nodosum here is attributed to the fungal antigen response, not to antifungal therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct seeding would place organisms in the lesion, but the biopsy shows no fungal elements.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hematogenous spread of the organism is dissemination, which the brick explicitly distinguishes from erythema nodosum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Latent reactivation is described for Histoplasma and Cryptococcus in the lungs, not as a cause of shin nodules.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man in Michigan is diagnosed with blastomycosis after a pneumonia that failed to respond to antibiotics. Which of the following is the most common site of dissemination in this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bone marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Central nervous system

choices.label: D
choices.text: Genitourinary tract

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skin

explanation.summary: Skin is the most common site of dissemination in blastomycosis, which matches the species name B. dermatitidis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Common sites of infection in blastomycosis are pulmonary (91 percent), skin (18 percent), bone (4 percent), genitourinary (2 percent), and central nervous system. Skin is the most common site of dissemination, which makes sense with the name Blastomyces dermatitidis. Skin lesions raise suspicion for blastomycosis, but their absence does not rule out the disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone is involved in about 4 percent of cases, far less often than skin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bone marrow spread through the reticuloendothelial system is emphasized for histoplasmosis, not blastomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Central nervous system involvement is the least common of the listed sites.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Genitourinary involvement occurs in roughly 2 percent of cases.

questions.stem: In patients diagnosed with blastomycosis, which of the following sites is involved in approximately 91 percent of cases?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Central nervous system

choices.label: C
choices.text: Genitourinary tract

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lungs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skin

explanation.summary: Blastomycosis is overwhelmingly a pulmonary disease, involving the lungs in about 91 percent of cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: The common sites of infection in blastomycosis are pulmonary (91 percent), skin (18 percent), bone (4 percent), genitourinary (2 percent), and central nervous system. Patients typically present with either an acute or chronic pneumonia with potential for dissemination, and only rarely present with dissemination without signs of pneumonia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone involvement occurs in roughly 4 percent of cases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Central nervous system involvement is the least common of the listed sites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Genitourinary involvement occurs in roughly 2 percent of cases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Skin is involved in about 18 percent of cases and is the most common site of dissemination, not the most common site overall.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old landscaper in Kentucky develops fever, malaise, cough, chest pain, and myalgias and is eventually diagnosed with acute pulmonary histoplasmosis. Which of the following best describes the usual interval between exposure and symptom onset?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 to 2 days after exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: 3 to 17 days after exposure

choices.label: C
choices.text: 6 to 12 hours after exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: 6 to 12 months after exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Within 24 hours of exposure

explanation.summary: Acute pulmonary histoplasmosis typically begins 3 to 17 days after exposure and mimics bacterial or viral pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Symptoms of acute pulmonary histoplasmosis usually present 3 to 17 days after exposure and resemble bacterial or viral pneumonias. Common symptoms include fever, malaise, cough, headache, chest pain, chills, and myalgias. Fewer than 1 percent of histoplasmosis cases require medical intervention, and the disease is frequently misdiagnosed as bacterial pneumonia until empiric antibiotics fail.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 1 to 2 day onset is shorter than the described interval.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An onset within hours suggests a toxin or hypersensitivity reaction, not acute histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Onset many months later reflects latent reactivation, not primary acute pulmonary disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Symptoms do not appear within a day; the brick gives a window of several days to a few weeks.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man from the Mississippi river valley with a 40 pack-year smoking history and emphysema has 4 months of productive cough and weight loss. Chest imaging shows upper lobe nodules with cavitation and hilar adenopathy. Sputum acid-fast smears are negative on three occasions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute pulmonary histoplasmosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disseminated histoplasmosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Erythema nodosum from coccidioidomycosis

explanation.summary: Slowly progressive cavitary lung disease in a smoker with underlying lung disease from an endemic area is chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Symptoms of chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis resemble the acute form but are slow and progressive, and as disease advances the pulmonary nodules can cavitate. Patients with pre-existing lung disease are at risk in addition to the immunosuppressed, and cancer belongs in the differential because smokers are at risk for both. The cavitation and adenopathy can mimic tuberculosis, which the negative acid-fast smears argue against.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute pulmonary histoplasmosis develops within days of exposure rather than over months of progressive decline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis presents with headache, altered mental status, and neck stiffness, not cavitary lung nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disseminated disease involves organs such as lymph nodes, skin, bone marrow, CNS, and GI tract in severely immunosuppressed patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Erythema nodosum is a skin finding on the shins and does not explain cavitary lung disease.

questions.stem: A severely immunosuppressed patient with histoplasmosis develops hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and pancytopenia. Which of the following routes best explains the spread of the fungus to these organs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascending spread along bronchial mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct extension across the pleural space

choices.label: C
choices.text: Retrograde spread along peripheral nerves

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spread through the lymphatics of the gut wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spread through the reticuloendothelial system

explanation.summary: Histoplasma disseminates through the reticuloendothelial system to liver, spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: After inhalation of conidia, the yeasts are phagocytized by macrophages in the lungs, replicate inside them, kill the macrophage, and spread to adjacent cells and phagocytes. In severe cases the infection disseminates beyond the lungs into multiple organ systems through the reticuloendothelial system, which includes the liver, spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow, producing exactly this combination of findings.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Spread along bronchial mucosa keeps the infection within the airways rather than reaching solid organs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct pleural extension would not account for lymph node, liver, spleen, and marrow involvement together.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neural spread is not a described mechanism for any of the geographically defined mycoses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gut lymphatic spread does not explain a primary pulmonary infection reaching the marrow and spleen.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman who lived in Indiana as a child but has lived in Oregon for 30 years begins a TNF-alpha inhibitor for rheumatoid arthritis. Three months later she develops fever and pulmonary nodules, and histoplasmosis is confirmed. Which of the following best explains her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An immune reaction to circulating fungal antigen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of colonizing yeast into a mold in the lung

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reactivation of a decades-old latent infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recent inhalation of conidia from Oregon soil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmission from another infected household member

explanation.summary: Histoplasma can persist latently inside macrophages for decades and reactivate when immunosuppression develops.
explanation.whyCorrect: Like M. tuberculosis, Histoplasma spp. can live inside the macrophages of patients and persist in the lungs for decades without symptoms. In patients who have lived in or traveled to endemic areas, disease can develop decades after the initial exposure, typically when immunosuppression occurs. TNF-alpha inhibitors are named in the brick as an immunosuppressive risk factor for severe disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An immune reaction to circulating antigen produces erythema nodosum, not pulmonary nodules with fever.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Histoplasma is a yeast at body temperature; it does not convert to mold inside the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma is concentrated in the Ohio and Mississippi river valleys rather than the Pacific Northwest.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Person-to-person transmission is not described for these environmentally acquired fungi.

questions.stem: Among the geographically defined mycoses discussed as causes of severe disease in the United States, which of the following organisms is most likely to infect the central nervous system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blastomyces gilchristii

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus neoformans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: All of these fungi can reach the CNS, but Cryptococcus spp. are the most likely to infect it.
explanation.whyCorrect: While all the fungi discussed in this brick can disseminate to the central nervous system, Cryptococcus spp. are the most likely to infect the CNS. The hallmark CNS manifestation is meningitis, which may extend into brain tissue as meningoencephalitis, and cryptococcomas can also occur in the brain as space-occupying lesions that resemble tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces reaches the CNS in only a small fraction of cases, well behind pulmonary and skin disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces gilchristii behaves like B. dermatitidis, for which CNS spread is uncommon.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides can disseminate to the CNS but is not the organism most likely to do so.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma can disseminate to the CNS but does so less often than Cryptococcus.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man with AIDS and a CD4 count of 40 cells/microliter has 10 days of worsening headache and confusion but no fever and no nuchal rigidity. CSF antigen testing is positive for Cryptococcus. Which of the following best explains the absence of classic meningeal signs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen assays detect colonization rather than disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cryptococcus does not invade the meninges

choices.label: C
choices.text: Meningeal signs appear only with bacterial meningitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Severe immunocompromise blunts the inflammatory response

choices.label: E
choices.text: The capsule blocks organism entry into the CSF

explanation.summary: In severely immunocompromised patients with cryptococcal meningitis, classic inflammatory signs may be absent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcal meningitis presents indistinguishably from bacterial meningitis, with fever, stiff neck, and altered mental status as the three most common presentations. However, in severely immunocompromised patients such as those with AIDS, classic signs of inflammation like fever or stiff neck may not be present, so special attention must be given to these patients when they have neurological symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antigen detection in CSF is the preferred diagnostic test for cryptococcal CNS disease, not a marker of colonization.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Meningitis is the hallmark CNS manifestation of cryptococcosis, so meningeal invasion clearly occurs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcal meningitis can produce the same meningeal signs as bacterial meningitis when the immune response is intact.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The capsule is a virulence structure and does not prevent the organism from reaching the CSF.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old immunocompetent man from coastal Oregon has a solitary 4 cm mass-like lung lesion that is initially thought to be a malignancy. Biopsy shows encapsulated yeast. Which of the following best describes this lesion and its most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A cavitary nodule caused by Histoplasma capsulatum

choices.label: B
choices.text: A cryptococcoma caused by Cryptococcus gattii

choices.label: C
choices.text: A spherule-filled granuloma caused by Coccidioides immitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: A verrucous lesion caused by Blastomyces dermatitidis

choices.label: E
choices.text: An erythema nodosum lesion caused by fungal antigen

explanation.summary: Nodular or mass-like cryptococcomas, especially with C. gattii, can mimic tuberculosis or malignancy on imaging.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pulmonary cryptococcal infection ranges from asymptomatic colonization to pneumonia. Nodules or mass-like lesions called cryptococcomas, especially with C. gattii, may mimic tuberculosis or malignancy on imaging. C. gattii is generally isolated to the West Coast of the United States and is associated with certain trees such as eucalyptus, which fits a coastal Oregon patient with encapsulated yeast on biopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma produces tiny narrow-based budding yeast, and its cavitary disease occurs in the river valley endemic zone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides produces spherules rather than encapsulated yeast and is concentrated in the desert Southwest.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Verrucous skin lesions are the dissemination pattern of blastomycosis, and its yeast is unencapsulated with broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Erythema nodosum is a skin reaction on the shins and cannot present as a lung mass.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisms discussed in this brick is the more common cause of cryptococcosis and is not restricted to a defined geographic region of the United States?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces gilchristii

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryptococcus gattii

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus neoformans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum

explanation.summary: C. neoformans is the more common cause of cryptococcosis and is not geographically defined; C. gattii is the West Coast species.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are the two main species that cause cryptococcosis. C. gattii is generally isolated to the West Coast of the United States and is associated with certain trees such as eucalyptus, while C. neoformans, the more common cause of cryptococcosis, is not geographically defined.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces gilchristii occupies the same defined central and eastern range as B. dermatitidis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides posadasii is confined to soil of the southwestern United States.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus gattii is the geographically defined species, restricted largely to the West Coast.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma capsulatum is concentrated in the Ohio and Mississippi river valleys within the United States.

questions.stem: A medical student is asked where most cases of coccidioidomycosis in the United States occur. Which of the following locations should the student give?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Southern Arizona and California's San Joaquin Valley

choices.label: B
choices.text: The northeastern United States and New England

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Ohio and Mississippi river valleys

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Pacific Northwest coast and its eucalyptus groves

choices.label: E
choices.text: The upper Midwest and Great Lakes states

explanation.summary: Coccidioidomycosis is concentrated in southern Arizona and California's southern San Joaquin Valley, hence Valley Fever.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coccidioides spp. live in the soil in the southwestern United States, and most cases of coccidioidomycosis occur in southern Arizona and California's southern San Joaquin Valley, which is the origin of the nickname Valley Fever. Working or recreating outdoors in these areas increases the risk of infection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The northeastern United States is not where the majority of coccidioidomycosis cases occur.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Ohio and Mississippi river valleys are the endemic area for Histoplasma spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The Pacific Northwest with eucalyptus association describes Cryptococcus gattii.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The upper Midwest and Great Lakes region falls within the Blastomyces range.

questions.stem: A public health officer is comparing exposure histories for two fungi whose geographic ranges overlap substantially in the central United States. Which of the following exposures is more characteristic of Blastomyces spp. than of Histoplasma spp.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleaning accumulated droppings from a chicken coop

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clearing decomposing leaves and rotting wood outdoors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Driving dirt roads through desert soil after a dust storm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exploring a cave heavily inhabited by bats

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pruning eucalyptus trees along the Pacific coast

explanation.summary: Blastomyces spp. favor soil with decomposing leaves or wood and, unlike Histoplasma, have no bat or bird dropping association.
