explanation.whyCorrect: Risk factors for blastomycosis are similar to those for histoplasmosis, and people who work outdoors are at elevated risk since Blastomyces spp. grow in the soil. However, Blastomyces spp. do not have an association with bat or bird droppings, in contrast to Histoplasma spp., and areas that have decomposing leaves or wood favor Blastomyces spp.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bird droppings enrich soil for Histoplasma spp., which is the organism this question is meant to exclude.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Desert soil dust exposure in the Southwest corresponds to Coccidioides spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bat droppings in caves are the classic spelunker exposure for Histoplasma spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Eucalyptus trees on the West Coast are the exposure associated with Cryptococcus gattii.

questions.stem: Serologic surveys of residents in areas where Histoplasma spp. are present show that 60 to 90 percent have antibodies against the fungus, yet most of these people have never been diagnosed with histoplasmosis. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody assays are too insensitive to detect true infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibody positivity reliably confirms active pulmonary infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exposure and infection are common but rarely cause serious disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Histoplasma antibodies are cross-reactions with common bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most residents have latent disease that will reactivate by age 55

explanation.summary: Widespread seropositivity without diagnosed disease shows that Histoplasma exposure is common while significant illness is rare.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serological testing of residents of areas where Histoplasma spp. are present shows that 60 to 90 percent have antibodies against the fungi, and most of these people have never been diagnosed with histoplasmosis. So while significant exposure or even infection is common, it rarely leads to significant disease. In immunocompetent patients the most likely outcome is asymptomatic infection or mild flu-like symptoms that resolve without medical intervention.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The problem with antibody testing is the 2 to 6 week delay in development, not failure to detect exposure in these surveys.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibody positivity here reflects past exposure in people who were never diagnosed, so it does not confirm active infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These assays detect antibodies generated against Histoplasma spp., not bacterial cross-reactions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactivation occurs only in a minority, typically when immunosuppression develops, not predictably by a given age.

questions.stem: Which of the following patients is at greatest risk for severe disease such as pneumonia or dissemination after exposure to Histoplasma spp.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 20-year-old healthy student visiting a cave once

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 25-year-old healthy hiker in the endemic region

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 30-year-old healthy poultry worker with prior exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 40-year-old healthy construction worker who smokes

choices.label: E
choices.text: A 62-year-old man with AIDS and a low CD4 count

explanation.summary: Severe histoplasmosis clusters in HIV/AIDS, patients over 55, infants, and the otherwise immunosuppressed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Severe disease, like pneumonia or dissemination, is more likely to occur in patients with HIV/AIDS, those over 55, infants, or those who are immunosuppressed. A 62-year-old man with AIDS meets two of these criteria at once. In immunocompetent patients the most likely outcome of exposure is asymptomatic infection or mild flu-like symptoms that resolve on their own.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A single cave exposure raises the chance of infection but not of severe disease in a healthy young person.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A healthy young adult would most likely have asymptomatic or mild self-limited infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Poultry work raises exposure risk, but immunocompetence keeps the risk of severe disease low.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Smoking is a risk factor for chronic pulmonary disease, but it is not the greatest risk for severe or disseminated infection here.

questions.stem: Two patients from the same endemic county acquire blastomycosis: one is otherwise healthy and one has AIDS and is taking glucocorticoids. The second patient develops far more severe disease. Which of the following principles best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AIDS patients acquire a more virulent Blastomyces species

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucocorticoids accelerate conversion to the mold form

choices.label: C
choices.text: Healthy patients clear the fungus with antibiotic therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior exposure protects healthy patients from reinfection

choices.label: E
choices.text: The level of immunosuppression correlates with disease severity

explanation.summary: In blastomycosis, the degree of immunosuppression directly correlates with how severe the disease becomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The risk factors for blastomycosis are the same as those for histoplasmosis, and children, pregnant individuals, and the immunosuppressed are at risk for disease. The level of immunosuppression directly correlates with disease severity, and patients who are HIV positive and have progressed to AIDS or who take immunosuppressants such as glucocorticoids and TNF-alpha inhibitors are at greatest risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both B. dermatitidis and B. gilchristii cause blastomycosis, and no species switch by host status is described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucocorticoids do not drive conversion to the mold form; the host is at 37 degrees C, where the yeast form predominates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibiotics do not treat fungal infection, and failure of empiric antibiotics is what raises suspicion for it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Protective immunity from prior exposure is not the mechanism the brick invokes for differing severity.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman in Arkansas is treated for community-acquired pneumonia with two successive courses of empiric antibiotics without improvement. Sputum bacterial cultures are negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next consideration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fungal infection endemic to her geographic region

choices.label: B
choices.text: A repeat chest radiograph to establish the diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: A second course of the same empiric antibiotic

choices.label: D
choices.text: An immune reaction to circulating fungal antigen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reassurance, as fungal pneumonia is too rare to pursue

explanation.summary: Failure of empiric antibiotics in a community-acquired pneumonia should prompt consideration of an endemic fungal cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: When a patient has a community-acquired infection like pneumonia and empiric antibiotics fail to cure them, you must ask why the empiric therapy failed: a viral infection, resistant bacteria, or a fungal infection. Location matters, since living in an endemic area increases the likelihood of exposure. These fungi belong low on the differential but should be kept in mind when the most common causes are ruled out.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Imaging of fungal pneumonia resembles other community-acquired pneumonias and cannot establish the diagnosis alone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Repeating a therapy that has already failed twice does not address why it failed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An immune reaction to circulating antigen explains erythema nodosum, not persistent pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rarity does not make these infections irrelevant, since for some patients they are a matter of life or death.

questions.stem: A reference laboratory reports growth of one of the two species that cause coccidioidomycosis. Which of the following pairs of organisms is being reported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis and Blastomyces gilchristii

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis and Coccidioides posadasii

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coccidioides immitis and Cryptococcus gattii

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Histoplasma capsulatum and Blastomyces dermatitidis

explanation.summary: Coccidioidomycosis is caused by Coccidioides immitis and Coccidioides posadasii.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two species cause coccidioidomycosis: Coccidioides immitis and Coccidioides posadasii. Both live in the soil of the southwestern United States, form arthroconidia in the mold phase at 25 degrees C, and convert to endospore-filled spherules in the host.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis and Blastomyces gilchristii are the two fungi that cause blastomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This pair mixes one Coccidioides species with a Cryptococcus species from a different disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are the two main species causing cryptococcosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This pair spans two different diseases, histoplasmosis and blastomycosis.

questions.stem: After a patient inhales Histoplasma conidia, alveolar macrophages phagocytize the organism. Which of the following best describes what happens next in the pathogenesis of histoplasmosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The conidia germinate into hyphae that invade blood vessels

choices.label: B
choices.text: The organism forms a thick capsule that blocks phagolysosomes

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism releases a toxin that lyses type II pneumocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The yeasts form spherules that rupture in alveolar spaces

choices.label: E
choices.text: The yeasts replicate inside macrophages and kill them

explanation.summary: Histoplasma survives and multiplies inside macrophages, killing them and spreading to adjacent phagocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: After inhalation of the conidia, the yeasts are phagocytized by macrophages in the lungs. Histoplasma spp. replicate in macrophages, eventually killing the macrophage and spreading to adjacent cells and phagocytes. This intracellular lifestyle is why the yeast can be seen inside macrophages and other white blood cells and why the organism can persist latently for decades.

whyWrongByChoice.A: At body temperature Histoplasma exists as a yeast; hyphal growth belongs to the 25 degrees C mold phase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A thick polysaccharide capsule is the hallmark of Cryptococcus spp., not Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No toxin-mediated destruction of pneumocytes is described for these fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spherule formation with endospore release is the tissue behavior of Coccidioides spp.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has an intensely itchy, scaly, ring-shaped patch on his forearm. A scraping grows a filamentous fungus that grows readily on dead, keratinized tissue. Which nutrient does this group of fungi prefer, and which secreted enzyme do they use to obtain it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chitin, broken down by secreted chitinase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collagen, broken down by secreted collagenase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen, broken down by secreted amylase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keratin, broken down by secreted keratinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sebum lipids, broken down by secreted lipase

explanation.summary: Dermatophytes feed on keratin using secreted keratinase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dermatophytes colonize keratinized tissues (skin, hair, and nails). Keratin is a structural protein of those tissues, and dermatophytes secrete keratinase to degrade keratin and use it as an energy source. This is why they stay confined to keratinized structures rather than invading deeper.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chitin is a component of the fungal cell wall itself, the target of calcofluor white stain, not a host nutrient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Collagen is a dermal protein; dermatophytes do not penetrate into the dermis and do not feed on collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycogen is the fungal cell-wall carbohydrate that PAS stain binds; it is not the nutrient dermatophytes harvest from the host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lipids are the preferred energy source of Malassezia spp., which is precisely why Malassezia is not classified as a dermatophyte.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman has an itchy, scaly annular rash on her trunk. There is no pus, no fluctuance, and no deep swelling. The infection is confined to the layer of dead, keratinized cells that shields the living epidermis from the environment. Which layer is involved?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Papillary dermis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reticular dermis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stratum basale

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stratum corneum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stratum spinosum

explanation.summary: Dermatophyte infections are limited to the stratum corneum, the outermost keratinized layer.
explanation.whyCorrect: The stratum corneum is made of dead, keratinized cells and protects healthy cells from the external environment. Dermatophytes impact only this outermost layer, which is why their infections are itchy and scaly rather than purulent or swollen the way deeper bacterial infections are.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dermatophytes do not penetrate into the dermis; dermal involvement would suggest a different organism such as S. schenckii.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The reticular dermis is deeper still and is unaffected in superficial dermatophyte infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The stratum basale is the deepest, actively dividing epidermal layer and is not colonized by dermatophytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The stratum spinosum lies deep to the granulosum and lucidum and contains living, non-keratinized cells.

questions.stem: A dermatologist wants to name the one dermatophyte genus that routinely causes disease in all three keratinized sites: skin, hair, and nails. Which genus fits that description?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton spp.

explanation.summary: Trichophyton spp. cause skin, hair, and nail infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the three dermatophyte genera, Trichophyton spp. are the ones described as causing skin, hair, and nail infections. This broad tissue range is why Trichophyton species appear as common causes of tinea corporis, cruris, pedis, barbae, capitis, and unguium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton spp. cause skin and nail infections but not hair infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are not dermatophytes at all; they use lipids and cause pityriasis versicolor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum spp. cause skin and hair infections and only rarely cause nail infections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii is a dimorphic fungus causing subcutaneous, lymphocutaneous disease, not a dermatophyte.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man has had recurrent tinea cruris and thickened, discolored toenails for years, but has never had scalp or beard involvement. Which dermatophyte genus characteristically infects skin and nails while sparing hair?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton spp.

explanation.summary: Epidermophyton spp. infect skin and nails, not hair.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epidermophyton spp. are listed as causing skin and nail infections only. Epidermophyton floccosum is among the most common causes of tinea cruris, tinea pedis, tinea corporis, and tinea unguium, but it does not figure among causes of the hair-bearing tineas.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are lipid-dependent yeasts causing pityriasis versicolor, not nail disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum spp. infect skin and hair and only rarely nails, the opposite of this pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii causes ulcerating nodules along lymphatics after skin puncture, not tinea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton spp. infect skin, hair, and nails, so hair-bearing sites would not be spared.

questions.stem: A microbiology instructor asks which dermatophyte genus is described as causing skin and hair infections while only rarely infecting nails. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton spp., which infect skin and nails

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia spp., which infect sebum-rich skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum spp., which infect skin and hair

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii, which infects lymphatics

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton spp., which infect skin, hair, nails

explanation.summary: Microsporum spp. cause skin and hair infections and rarely nail infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microsporum spp. are described as causing skin and hair infections, rarely causing nail infections. This matches their clinical profile: Microsporum canis is a frequent cause of tinea capitis and of tinea corporis among pet owners, but it is not on the list of common onychomycosis pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton spp. spare hair entirely, so they do not match a skin-and-hair pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are not dermatophytes and cause pityriasis versicolor on sebum-rich skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii is not a dermatophyte and spreads along lymphatic channels after inoculation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton spp. routinely infect nails as well, so nail infection is not rare for them.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old has an expanding lesion on the shoulder with an inflamed, red, scaly advancing border and skin in the center that looks nearly normal. Which mechanism best explains this ring-shaped appearance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keratinase is secreted only at the leading edge and never within the older central skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neutrophilic pus accumulates centrally and lifts the infected scale off the skin surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scratching mechanically strips the infected stratum corneum away from the lesion center

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fungus exhausts available keratin centrally and then migrates outward to fresh tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: The immune response partially clears the center while the fungus keeps spreading outward

explanation.summary: Central clearing results from the immune system clearing the center while the infection spreads peripherally.
explanation.whyCorrect: As a tinea lesion spreads, the immune system fights the infection and partially clears it in the center while the infection continues to spread outward. The result is centralized clearing with an inflamed, red, scaly advancing border, which is what gives tinea lesions their ring appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Keratinase secretion is how dermatophytes feed throughout the lesion; it is not restricted to the border.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dermatophyte infections are characteristically non-purulent; pus suggests bacterial co-infection instead.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Scratching causes breaks in the skin that admit bacteria; it does not create the ring morphology.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratin is not depleted; the stratum corneum is continuously renewed and there is no described nutrient-exhaustion mechanism.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old collegiate wrestler has an itchy, red, scaly eruption with an advancing border involving the groin, inner thighs, and scrotum. Which tinea infection does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tinea barbae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tinea corporis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tinea cruris

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tinea manuum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tinea pedis

explanation.summary: Tinea cruris is jock itch, the dermatophyte infection of the groin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinea cruris (jock itch) affects the groin and surrounding regions and can involve the thighs, buttocks, and scrotum. It is common in athletes because the thighs rub together during exercise and cause skin damage, increasing the likelihood of infection; tight-fitting clothing contributes for the same reason.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tinea barbae affects the beard area of the face.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tinea corporis is ringworm of the body; it can occur near folds but is not the groin-specific name.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea manuum is infection of the hands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinea pedis is athlete's foot, affecting the feet, typically starting between the toes.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman has thick, discolored, brittle toenails, and the junction between the nail and the surrounding skin has become disconnected. This infection is also known as onychomycosis. What is the corresponding tinea name?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tinea barbae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tinea capitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tinea corporis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tinea manuum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tinea unguium

explanation.summary: Tinea unguium is nail infection, also called onychomycosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinea unguium is the dermatophyte infection of the nails, also called onychomycosis. It is characterized by thick, discolored nails that may become brittle and break off, and the intersection between the nail and surrounding skin may become disconnected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tinea barbae affects the beard area.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tinea capitis is scalp infection, most common in children.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tinea corporis is ringworm of the body.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea manuum is infection of the hands, not of the nail plate itself.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has an inflamed, scaly scalp patch with irregular, patchy hair loss. On close inspection the hairs in the affected area are short and stubby and appear as black dots at the scalp surface. Which mechanism explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Comedones form as excess sebum plugs the openings of the hair follicles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhage into the hair follicles is caused by vigorous, repeated scratching

choices.label: C
choices.text: Melanin granules are deposited into the follicular openings by the fungus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pigmented fungal colonies grow outward on the surface of the scalp skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The fungus infects the hair, making it brittle so it breaks before growing out

explanation.summary: Black dots in tinea capitis are hairs made brittle by fungal invasion that break off at the scalp.
explanation.whyCorrect: In tinea capitis, the fungus infects the hair itself, making it brittle so that it breaks off before it can grow out. The residual short, stubby hairs appear as black dots. The associated hair loss is irregular and patchy and is temporary with prompt treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sebum plugging produces comedones, which is a feature of acne rather than dermatophyte infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Scratching can break the skin and admit bacteria but does not produce the black-dot hair pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no described fungal deposition of melanin into follicles in tinea capitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The appearance comes from broken hair shafts, not surface colonies of pigmented fungus.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has scaly scalp patches with central clearing, an advancing red border, and broken-off hairs. He sleeps with the family dog. A Wood's lamp examination is positive, and a KOH preparation with stain shows microconidia and rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia. Which organism is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton floccosum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia globosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum canis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trichophyton rubrum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton verrucosum

explanation.summary: A pet-associated, Wood's-lamp-positive tinea capitis with spindle-shaped macroconidia is Microsporum canis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microsporum canis is the dermatophyte that commonly comes from pets, it fluoresces under a Wood's lamp, and Microsporum spp. show rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia with microconidia present. Scalp infections are most frequently caused by Trichophyton and Microsporum species, and tinea capitis is most common in children.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton produces smooth, club-shaped macroconidia with no microconidia, and it does not infect hair.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia globosa causes pityriasis versicolor and shows yeast with short hyphae, not macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trichophyton spp. show cigar-shaped macroconidia with spiraled hyphae, not spindle-shaped macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton verrucosum is acquired from livestock and is the usual cause of tinea barbae in farmers.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old dairy farmer has itchy, red, crusted lesions in his beard area with patchy loss of beard hair. He handles cattle daily and has no rodent exposure. Which organism is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton floccosum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia furfur

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum canis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trichophyton mentagrophytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton verrucosum

explanation.summary: Trichophyton verrucosum causes livestock-associated tinea barbae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trichophyton verrucosum causes infections in livestock, and in farmers and others who work with livestock it is the most common cause of tinea barbae. Tinea barbae presents with itchy, red, crusted lesions of the beard area and, like tinea capitis, can cause hair loss in the affected area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton floccosum does not infect hair and so is not a cause of tinea barbae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia furfur is a lipid-dependent yeast causing pityriasis versicolor, not beard infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum canis is the pet-associated dermatophyte, typically from dogs and cats rather than cattle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trichophyton mentagrophytes is shed by rodents and is more common in urban environments.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has itchy, macerated, scaly skin between his fourth and fifth toes. Which clinical form of tinea pedis is this, and how common is it relative to the others?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interdigital (toe web) form, the least common form

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interdigital (toe web) form, the most common form

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moccasin (chronic hyperkeratotic) form, the most common form

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ulcerative form, the most common form

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesiculobullous form, the most common form

explanation.summary: The interdigital (toe web) form is the most common presentation of tinea pedis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinea pedis typically starts between the toes and extends outward. The interdigital, or toe web, form is listed as the most common presentation, predominantly involving the skin between the toes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The site is correctly identified but the frequency is wrong; the interdigital form is the most common.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The moccasin form is a recognized presentation but is not the most common one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ulceration is a rare complication of tinea pedis, mostly in immunocompromised and diabetic patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vesiculobullous form produces painful, itchy blisters and is not the most common form.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has chronic, itchy, flaky disease of both soles in which the skin has become thick, dry, and scaly, resembling a worn-down piece of footwear. Which form of tinea pedis does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interdigital (toe web) form

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intertrigo of the toe webs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moccasin (hyperkeratotic) form

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tinea unguium of the toenails

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesiculobullous blistering form

explanation.summary: Thick, dry, scaly soles resembling a worn moccasin define the chronic hyperkeratotic form of tinea pedis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the moccasin, or chronic hyperkeratotic, form of tinea pedis the skin becomes thick, dry, and scaly, looking like a worn-down moccasin, and it is itchy and flaky. The soles of the feet are among the areas most commonly affected in tinea pedis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The interdigital form predominantly involves the skin between the toes rather than the whole sole.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intertrigo is inflammation from two skin surfaces rubbing together, not hyperkeratotic sole scaling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea unguium affects the nail plate, producing thick discolored nails rather than sole scaling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vesiculobullous form produces fluid-filled blisters with marked redness and swelling.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old runner develops painful, itchy, fluid-filled blisters on the soles of both feet. The surrounding skin is very red and swollen. Which form of tinea pedis is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interdigital (toe web) form

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intertrigo between the toes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moccasin (hyperkeratotic) form

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tinea manuum of the palm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesiculobullous form

explanation.summary: Painful, itchy blisters on the soles with marked redness and swelling define vesiculobullous tinea pedis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The vesiculobullous form of tinea pedis produces fluid-filled blisters on the soles or elsewhere. The blisters are painful and itchy and the area is typically very red and swollen. Note that these forms are not mutually exclusive and can occur simultaneously in the same patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The interdigital form is scaling and maceration between the toes, without bullae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intertrigo is friction-related inflammation of apposed skin surfaces, not a blistering tinea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The moccasin form produces thick, dry, scaly skin rather than blisters.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea manuum is infection of the hands, not of the soles of the feet.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus has long-standing athlete's foot that has now ulcerated. He is at greatest risk for which of the following complications?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deep tissue bacterial infection entering through the ulcerated skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulomatous nodules tracking along the draining lymphatic channels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypopigmented, finely scaly patches spreading proximally up the leg

choices.label: D
choices.text: Permanent destruction of the hair follicles on the dorsum of the foot

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic dissemination of the dermatophyte through the bloodstream

explanation.summary: Ulcerated tinea pedis in a diabetic or immunocompromised patient risks deep bacterial infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: In rare cases tinea pedis causes ulceration, which leads to deep tissue infection by bacteria; this predominantly occurs in immunocompromised and diabetic patients. The dermatophyte itself stays superficial, but the breach in the skin barrier is the entry point bacteria exploit.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nodules along lymphatics are the chain-of-pearls pattern of sporotrichosis, not of tinea pedis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypopigmented scaly patches describe pityriasis versicolor caused by Malassezia spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Permanent hair loss is not a described outcome; tinea-related hair loss is temporary with treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dermatophytes remain confined to keratinized tissue and do not disseminate hematogenously.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old with an itchy tinea corporis lesion he has been scratching for weeks now has pus and deep, tender swelling at the site. Which organisms most likely account for this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans or Malassezia globosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clostridium perfringens or Bacteroides fragilis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Serratia marcescens

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii or Microsporum canis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Pus and deep swelling in a tinea lesion suggest bacterial co-infection with S. aureus or S. pyogenes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pus and deep tissue swelling are not typical of dermatophyte infection. When they occur, it may be due to co-infection with a bacterium like S. aureus or S. pyogenes: damage caused by the dermatophyte and by scratching creates tiny breaks in the skin that bacteria use to start an infection. This is why prompt treatment of tinea is emphasized.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These are fungi; they would not explain a new purulent, deep bacterial-type inflammatory process.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anaerobes are not implicated in secondary infection of superficial tinea lesions here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These Gram-negative organisms are not the described secondary invaders of tinea lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both are fungi, and dermatophytes characteristically do not produce pus or deep swelling.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has had untreated athlete's foot for over a year. He now has thick, discolored toenails on the same foot. He lives alone and has no pets. Which mode of spread best explains the new nail involvement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoinoculation from his own untreated foot infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct contact with an infected person in the household

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct contact with an infected pet living in the household

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding of the nail bed from the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Indirect contact with a contaminated locker room floor

explanation.summary: Dermatophytes spread from one body site to another in the same patient by autoinoculation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transmission of dermatophytes occurs through direct contact with an infected person or pet, indirect contact, or autoinoculation. Infected patients shed dermatophytes into their environment and can further infect themselves; a foot infection may progress to a nail infection, which is why prompt treatment and stopping spread are essential.

whyWrongByChoice.B: He lives alone, so person-to-person direct contact is not the explanation here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: He has no pets, so pet-to-person transmission cannot account for the new infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dermatophytes stay within keratinized tissue and do not travel through the bloodstream.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Indirect environmental contact could have started the original tinea pedis but not this site-to-site spread.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman has confirmed tinea unguium of several toenails that has not responded to topical therapy. Which statement best describes the treatment consideration for nail infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A brief course of topical antifungal applied to the nail plate is curative

choices.label: B
choices.text: A topical antibacterial agent under an occlusive nail dressing is used

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation alone is appropriate, as nail infections clear spontaneously

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged oral antifungal therapy is needed, with more severe side effects

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical debridement alone, with no antifungal agent, is the standard

explanation.summary: Nail infections resist topical therapy and require prolonged oral antifungals with greater toxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nail infections are resistant to topical treatment and may require prolonged oral antifungal therapy. These oral antifungals have more severe side effects than their topical counterparts, which is exactly why stopping an infection such as tinea pedis before it spreads to the nails is preferred.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topical therapy is described as inadequate for nail infection, which is the central point here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The pathogen is fungal, so an antibacterial agent does not treat the infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Untreated infections spread further rather than resolving on their own.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Debridement without antifungal therapy is not the described management of onychomycosis.

questions.stem: A biopsy of an ulcerating nodule shows granulomatous inflammation, and within a giant cell there is a yeast surrounded by a radiating, star-shaped eosinophilic pattern. This inclusion is most characteristic of which infection, and in which setting is it most often seen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pityriasis versicolor, most often seen after sun exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sporotrichosis, most often seen in disseminated disease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tinea capitis, most often seen in school-aged children

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tinea corporis, most often seen in pet-owning adults

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tinea unguium, most often seen in elderly patients

explanation.summary: Asteroid bodies are star-shaped inclusions around yeast in the granulomas of sporotrichosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sporotrichosis infections are characterized by granulomatous inflammation. Asteroid bodies, which show a star-shaped pattern around the yeast, can sometimes be found within the giant cells of the granuloma, and they are found more often in disseminated disease than in cutaneous forms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pityriasis versicolor is a superficial, non-granulomatous infection diagnosed by scale, not biopsy inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tinea capitis is a superficial dermatophyte infection of the scalp without granuloma formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea corporis is confined to the stratum corneum and does not generate giant-cell granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinea unguium involves the keratinized nail plate and does not produce tissue granulomas.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old restaurant dishwasher who keeps her hands submerged in water for hours and bites her nails presents with a red, tender, swollen infection of the skin surrounding one nail bed. What is this condition called?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intertrigo

choices.label: B
choices.text: Onychomycosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Paronychia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporotrichosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tinea manuum

explanation.summary: Paronychia is infection of the skin surrounding the nail bed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Paronychia is an infection of the skin surrounding the nailbed. Risk factors include overzealous manicuring, nail biting, trauma, frequent submersion of the hand in water, and fungal infections. Fungal nail infections can cause the skin around the nail bed to disconnect, giving bacteria such as S. aureus and S. pyogenes an opportunity to infect the nailbed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Intertrigo is inflammation where two skin surfaces rub together, such as the groin or under the breasts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Onychomycosis is fungal infection of the nail plate itself, producing thick, discolored nails.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporotrichosis follows a skin puncture with contaminated plant material and tracks along lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinea manuum is a dermatophyte infection of the hand skin, not of the nail fold.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman with obesity has red, irritated, inflamed skin under her breasts and within her abdominal folds where skin surfaces rub against one another. Which condition best describes this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intertrigo

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pityriasis versicolor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sporotrichosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tinea capitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tinea unguium

explanation.summary: Intertrigo is inflammation of skin folds caused by two skin surfaces rubbing together.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intertrigo is an inflammatory condition that occurs in skin folds, where two skin surfaces rub against each other, leading to irritation, inflammation, and sometimes infection. It is most common in the groin, armpits, under the breasts, between the toes, and in abdominal folds in people who are overweight or obese, and the resulting skin damage makes bacterial and fungal infection more likely.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pityriasis versicolor produces hypo- or hyperpigmented finely scaly patches on sebum-rich trunk skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sporotrichosis follows traumatic inoculation with plant material and forms nodules along lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea capitis is scalp infection with scaling and patchy hair loss, typically in children.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinea unguium is a nail infection producing thick, discolored, brittle nails.

questions.stem: A student wants to lower his risk of acquiring tinea pedis. Which behavior would most increase his risk if he continued it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Changing out of damp clothing right after finishing a run

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treating his dog's ringworm promptly and cleaning its bed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Walking barefoot in the public gym shower and locker room

choices.label: D
choices.text: Washing skin folds promptly after a heavy sweating session

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wearing loose, non-restrictive clothing while exercising

explanation.summary: Public showers, pools, and locker rooms are commonly contaminated with dermatophytes, and barefoot walking is a major cause of athlete's foot.
explanation.whyCorrect: Public places like swimming pools, locker rooms, and gym showers are commonly contaminated with dermatophytes; this is an extremely common cause of athlete's foot, so walking around barefoot in these areas should be avoided. Warm, humid environments and close living quarters are further environmental risk factors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Changing out of moist clothes removes the warm, moist conditions dermatophytes need.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Treating an infected pet and cleaning the areas it frequents reduces environmental dermatophyte load.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cleaning the skin promptly after sweating and attending to skin folds is a recommended preventive step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loose clothing is protective; tight clothing causes friction that promotes tinea cruris and corporis.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl has a scaly scalp patch with broken hairs. A Wood's lamp examination of the scalp shows no fluorescence. Which is the best interpretation of this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A dermatophyte infection has been reliably excluded by this result

choices.label: B
choices.text: A fungal infection is still possible, as not all species fluoresce

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fluorescence appears only after the sample is treated with KOH

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lesion must therefore be bacterial rather than fungal in origin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The result confirms Microsporum canis as the causative organism

explanation.summary: A negative Wood's lamp does not rule out a fungal infection, because not all dermatophytes fluoresce.
explanation.whyCorrect: A Wood's lamp uses ultraviolet light to make certain dermatophytes fluoresce; Microsporum canis, for example, glows under a Wood's lamp. However, not all dermatophytes fluoresce under a Wood's light, so a negative test cannot rule out a fungal infection. Most superficial fungal infections are in fact diagnosed by sight and clinical presentation alone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Exclusion is exactly what a negative Wood's lamp cannot do, since many species do not fluoresce.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lamp is applied directly to skin and hair; KOH is a separate microscopy preparation step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A non-fluorescing dermatophyte remains the most likely cause given scaling and broken hairs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Microsporum canis is the classic fluorescing species, so a negative result argues against it, not for it.

questions.stem: A culture from a scaly groin lesion grows a mold showing smooth, club-shaped macroconidia arranged in clusters of two to three, with no microconidia seen. Which genus does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton spp.

explanation.summary: Smooth, club-shaped macroconidia in clusters of 2-3 with no microconidia identify Epidermophyton spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epidermophyton spp. produce smooth, club-shaped macroconidia, likened to a beaver's tail, in clusters of two to three, and they produce no microconidia. Since these dermatophytes exist only as molds, the appearance of the mold and its conidia is how the genera are distinguished.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are yeasts that show clustered yeast cells with short hyphal elements.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum spp. show rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia with microconidia present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii is thermally dimorphic and appears as cigar-shaped yeast in patient samples.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton spp. show cigar-shaped macroconidia with microconidia present and spiraled hyphae.

questions.stem: Microscopy of a dermatophyte culture shows cigar-shaped macroconidia, numerous microconidia, and hyphae that form coils or spirals. Which genus is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton spp.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton spp.

explanation.summary: Cigar-shaped macroconidia with microconidia and spiraled hyphae identify Trichophyton spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trichophyton spp. are described by cigar-shaped macroconidia, the presence of microconidia, and coiled or spiraled hyphae. Trichophyton is the genus that infects skin, hair, and nails, so this morphology can turn up in scrapings from almost any tinea site.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton spp. produce smooth, club-shaped macroconidia and no microconidia at all.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are yeasts and do not produce macroconidia or spiraled hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum spp. produce rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia rather than cigar-shaped ones.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii yeast forms are cigar-shaped, but it forms no macroconidia in patient samples.

questions.stem: A laboratory subcultures an isolate that has been identified as a Microsporum species. Which microscopic appearance should be expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding yeast cells mixed with short, curved hyphal fragments in clumps

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cigar-shaped macroconidia with microconidia and coil or spiraled hyphae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cigar-shaped yeast forms with occasional star-shaped inclusion material

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia, with microconidia present

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smooth, club-shaped macroconidia in clusters, with no microconidia

explanation.summary: Microsporum spp. show rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia with microconidia present.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microsporum spp. are identified by rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia, with microconidia present. Recognizing this morphology is what allowed identification of Microsporum in the boy with the pet dog, whose scraping showed microconidia and spindle-shaped macroconidia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Yeast cells with short hyphae describe Malassezia spp. in a KOH preparation of skin scale.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cigar-shaped macroconidia with spiraled hyphae describe Trichophyton spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cigar-shaped yeast with asteroid bodies describes Sporothrix schenckii in patient tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: That is the Epidermophyton pattern, which notably lacks microconidia altogether.

questions.stem: A laboratory cultures a skin scraping from a patient with tinea corporis at both 25°C and 37°C. Which result should be expected, and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mold at 25°C and yeast at 37°C, because dermatophytes are dimorphic

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mold at both temperatures, because dermatophytes have no yeast form

choices.label: C
choices.text: No growth at either temperature, because these fungi cannot be cultured

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yeast at 25°C and mold at 37°C, the reverse of dimorphic fungi

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast at both temperatures, because dermatophytes have no mold form

explanation.summary: Epidermophyton, Trichophyton, and Microsporum are not dimorphic; they exist only as molds.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epidermophyton, Trichophyton, and Microsporum spp. are not dimorphic. They only exist in a mold form and have no single-celled yeast form, so temperature does not switch their morphology. It is the appearance of this mold form and its conidia that is used to distinguish the genera.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Temperature-driven mold-to-yeast conversion describes S. schenckii, which is thermally dimorphic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dermatophytes are culturable, most commonly on Sabouraud dextrose agar.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No fungus in this brick shows this inverted pattern, and dermatophytes do not convert at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dermatophytes do have a mold form; it is the yeast form they lack.

questions.stem: Before examining a skin scraping under the microscope, a technician treats it with a 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution. What does the KOH accomplish?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds chitin, making fungi fluoresce under UV light

choices.label: B
choices.text: It dissolves human tissue, leaving the fungi behind

choices.label: C
choices.text: It kills the dermatophyte before it can be examined

choices.label: D
choices.text: It raises the pH so that bacteria cannot overgrow it

choices.label: E
choices.text: It stains the fungal cell wall a deep magenta color

explanation.summary: KOH is not a stain; it dissolves host tissue so the fungi stand out.
explanation.whyCorrect: KOH (10-20% solution) is not a stain but it dissolves human tissue, leaving the fungi behind and easier to see. Taking a scraping from infected skin or nails and applying KOH removes the scraped dead host cells and isolates the fungi, making identification easier. Because KOH adds no color, it is typically followed by a stain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding chitin and cellulose to produce UV fluorescence describes calcofluor white stain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The purpose is clearing host material for visualization, not killing the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A low pH is what makes Sabouraud agar selective against bacteria; KOH is a microscopy reagent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Magenta staining of fungal cell-wall glycogen is the periodic acid-Schiff stain, not KOH.

questions.stem: A pathologist wants a stain that binds the glycogen in the fungal cell wall and turns the organisms magenta in a tissue section. Which stain should be requested?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calcofluor white stain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gomori methenamine silver stain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Periodic acid-Schiff stain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Potassium hydroxide preparation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sabouraud dextrose agar culture

explanation.summary: PAS binds fungal cell-wall glycogen and turns the fungi magenta.
explanation.whyCorrect: The periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain binds the glycogen in the fungi's cell wall, turning it a magenta color. It is one of three stains commonly used after a KOH preparation to visualize these fungi, alongside Gomori methenamine silver and calcofluor white.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcofluor white binds chitin and cellulose in the fungal cell, causing fluorescence under UV light.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GMS reacts with silver ions in the fungal cell wall, reducing them and causing a black precipitate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: KOH adds no color at all; it dissolves host tissue and must be followed by a stain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sabouraud agar is a culture medium, not a staining method for visualizing fungi in a sample.

questions.stem: A microbiology lab plates a nail scraping on Sabouraud dextrose agar to grow the suspected dermatophyte. What makes this medium selective for fungi?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It contains an antibacterial antibiotic added to the medium

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is incubated at a temperature that bacteria cannot tolerate

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is prepared anaerobically, which kills contaminating bacteria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its high dextrose content cannot be used by human bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its low pH, around 5.6, inhibits the growth of most bacteria

explanation.summary: Sabouraud dextrose agar is selective because of its low pH of about 5.6, which inhibits bacterial growth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several agars can be used to grow fungi, but the most commonly used is Sabouraud dextrose agar, usually shortened to Sabouraud agar. It is selective due to its low pH: Sabouraud agar has a pH around 5.6, which inhibits bacterial growth while permitting fungi to grow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Selectivity here is attributed to the acidity of the medium rather than to an added antibiotic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Many bacteria grow well at fungal incubation temperatures, so temperature alone is not selective.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The medium is not anaerobic, and anaerobiosis would not selectively favor fungal growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dextrose is a readily usable carbon source for bacteria as well, so it cannot confer selectivity.

questions.stem: Malassezia spp. cause superficial skin infections but are not classified as dermatophytes. Which feature best explains this distinction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are bacteria rather than true fungal organisms of the skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are transmitted only by direct contact with an infected pet

choices.label: C
choices.text: They cannot be grown or identified in a clinical laboratory at all

choices.label: D
choices.text: They invade the dermis rather than remaining in the stratum corneum

choices.label: E
choices.text: They use lipids rather than keratin as their preferred energy source

explanation.summary: Malassezia spp. use lipids, not keratin, which is why they are not dermatophytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The answer is their energy source: dermatophytes have keratin as their preferred energy source, while Malassezia spp. use lipids. Malassezia spp. are usually commensal yeasts living on skin with high sebum production, including the scalp, face, chest, and back, and they produce hyphae and cause pathology when triggered by skin damage such as sunburn, immunosuppression, or excess sebum production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Malassezia spp. are fungi, specifically yeasts, not bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia are commensals already present on human skin, not pet-acquired pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: They can be confirmed with a KOH preparation and staining, showing yeast cells and short hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pityriasis versicolor is a superficial infection; deeper spread is characteristic of S. schenckii.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman returns from a beach vacation, where she spent long days in the sun and got a tan. She now has mildly itchy, hypopigmented, finely scaly patches across her upper back and chest. Which organism is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton floccosum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia globosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum canis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton rubrum

explanation.summary: Hypo- or hyperpigmented finely scaly trunk patches appearing after tanning are pityriasis versicolor from Malassezia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malassezia spp. cause pityriasis versicolor, characterized by hypo- or hyperpigmented, finely scaly patches on the trunk and shoulders that may be itchy, and M. globosa causes the most infections. Pityriasis versicolor commonly presents after tanning, because sun damage to the skin combined with heat-driven excess sebum production promotes Malassezia growth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton floccosum causes scaly, itchy tinea of skin and nails, not pigment change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum canis causes pet-associated tinea capitis and corporis with ring-shaped lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii causes ulcerating nodules after skin puncture, not scaly trunk patches.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton rubrum is a dermatophyte; dermatophytes do not cause pigmentary versicolor patches.

questions.stem: A KOH preparation with stain is made from a scraping of hypopigmented, finely scaly patches on a patient's back. Which microscopic finding is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cigar-shaped macroconidia together with numerous small microconidia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cigar-shaped yeast forms surrounded by radiating star-shaped inclusions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clustered yeast cells with short hyphae, a spaghetti-and-meatballs look

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia among branching septate hyphae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smooth, club-shaped macroconidia arranged in clusters of two or three

explanation.summary: Malassezia scrapings show yeast cells plus short hyphae: spaghetti and meatballs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malassezia spp. can be confirmed with a potassium hydroxide preparation with staining. Under the microscope, scraping of lesions shows both yeast cells and short hyphal elements, producing the classic spaghetti-and-meatballs appearance: the clustered yeast cells resemble meatballs and the hyphae resemble spaghetti.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cigar-shaped macroconidia with microconidia identify Trichophyton spp.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cigar-shaped yeast with asteroid bodies is seen in sporotrichosis tissue, not versicolor scale.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spindle-shaped macroconidia are the hallmark of Microsporum spp., a dermatophyte genus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Smooth, club-shaped macroconidia in clusters identify Epidermophyton spp.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man with advanced HIV/AIDS who works in landscaping develops pulmonary disease and then systemic illness caused by a fungus normally associated with localized skin nodules. How did this unusual presentation most likely arise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoinoculation from an untreated tinea pedis infection of the foot

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct contact with an infected pet that had been shedding the fungus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous spread from a colonized, lipid-rich area of scalp skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhalation of spores, which rarely causes pulmonary and systemic disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Puncture of the skin by a thorn, with spread along lymphatic channels

explanation.summary: Rarely, inhaled Sporothrix spores cause pulmonary sporotrichosis and systemic dissemination, especially in advanced immunodeficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sporotrichosis is usually acquired when the skin is punctured and contaminated with S. schenckii, producing the lymphocutaneous form. However, inhalation of spores rarely leads to pulmonary sporotrichosis and systemic dissemination, particularly in patients with advanced immunodeficiency such as HIV/AIDS, which fits this landscaper's exposure and immune status.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoinoculation spreads dermatophytes between keratinized sites and does not cause pulmonary disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pet contact transmits Microsporum canis, a superficial dermatophyte, not a systemic fungus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipid-rich scalp colonization describes Malassezia, which does not disseminate this way here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thorn puncture is the classic route, but it produces the lymphocutaneous form, not pulmonary disease.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old gardener who was pricked by a thorn while handling mulch has a red papule on her thumb that enlarged into a firm nodule and then ulcerated. Several smaller nodules have since appeared in a chain up her forearm. Which organism is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton floccosum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia furfur

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum canis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporothrix schenckii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton rubrum

explanation.summary: An ulcerating nodule after plant-material inoculation with secondary nodules along the lymphatics is lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sporothrix schenckii, the cause of Rose Handler's disease, is transmitted when skin is punctured and contaminated with the fungus from decaying vegetation such as moss or mulch. The most common presentation is the lymphocutaneous form: infection begins as a small red papule that enlarges into a firm nodule that may ulcerate, and secondary nodules develop along the lymphatics, producing the classic chain-of-pearls appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton floccosum causes tinea of the skin and nails without deep or lymphatic spread.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia furfur causes pityriasis versicolor with finely scaly pigment changes on the trunk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum canis causes pet-associated tinea of skin and hair, not lymphatic nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton rubrum causes superficial tinea confined to the stratum corneum and nails.

questions.stem: Material is obtained from the ulcerating thumb nodule of a gardener with suspected sporotrichosis and examined after KOH treatment and staining. Which form of the organism is expected in this patient sample, and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cigar-shaped yeast, because the organism is a yeast at body heat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Club-shaped macroconidia, arranged in clusters of two to three

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clustered yeast with short hyphae, in a spaghetti-like pattern

choices.label: D
choices.text: Septate mold hyphae, because the organism is a mold at body heat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spindle-shaped macroconidia, with rough outer walls and spirals

explanation.summary: S. schenckii is thermally dimorphic: a mold at 25°C and a cigar-shaped yeast at 37°C in patient samples.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sporothrix schenckii is a thermally dimorphic fungus that is a mold in the cold (25°C, the environment) and a yeast in the heat (37°C, patient samples). A combination of KOH and staining reveals the cigar-shaped yeast present in patient samples, although culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Club-shaped macroconidia in small clusters identify Epidermophyton spp., a dermatophyte.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Yeast with short hyphae in a spaghetti-and-meatballs pattern identifies Malassezia spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mold form appears at the cooler environmental temperature, not at body temperature.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia identify Microsporum spp., a dermatophyte.
